# EzyFusion — Component Inventory v0.2 (REVISED, awaiting approval to implement)

Companion to `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` v0.2. The initial inventory is **15 components**. Anything else is added **only when a real requirement needs it** (see §C for the trigger of each deferred item). Nothing here is implemented yet.

Source legend: `shadcn` = generated by the shadcn CLI (only the two edits allowed by DESIGN_SYSTEM §4.1 / §12.2: size variants and focus classes) · `compose` = thin wrapper over shadcn parts · `custom` = small hand-written component.

## A. Initial inventory (exactly 15)

### A1. shadcn primitives (9)

| # | Component | Source | Purpose | Spec notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Button` | shadcn | All actions | Sizes `default` (h-10) and `icon` (size-10) only; `sm` removed; solid focus ring; loading = `disabled` + `aria-busy` + spinner |
| 2 | `Input` | shadcn | Text, search, numeric text | `h-10`, `border-input`, 16px below `md`; native `<label>` (no shadcn `Label` initially); `maxLength` where bounded |
| 3 | `Select` | shadcn | Enum fields, simple filters, page size | Trigger `h-10`, items `min-h-10`; labelled by a visible `<label>` |
| 4 | `Card` | shadcn | Content container | Never nested |
| 5 | `Table` | shadcn | Data tables | Used directly; no `DataTable` wrapper; `caption` sr-only; `scope="col"` |
| 6 | `Pagination` | shadcn | Table footer | Links/buttons `size-10`; page size from the whitelist |
| 7 | `Alert` | shadcn | Persistent inline info/error/success | `role="alert"` for errors, `role="status"` otherwise; destructive variant uses `destructive-subtle*` tokens where on tint |
| 8 | `Sheet` | shadcn | Mobile navigation (if navigation exists) | Radix focus trap, `Esc` closes, focus returns to trigger |
| 9 | `DropdownMenu` | shadcn | Row actions, user menu | Items `min-h-10`; trigger has `sr-only` text |

### A2. Shared components (6)

| # | Component | Source | Purpose | Props (sketch) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | `StatusBadge` | compose over shadcn `badge`* | Tone + icon + text | `tone: "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" \| "info" \| "neutral"`, `children` |
| 11 | `PageHeader` | custom | `h1` + description + actions | `title`, `description?`, `actions?` |
| 12 | `EmptyState` | compose (`Card`-style layout) | "Nothing yet" / "no results" | `icon`, `title`, `description?`, `action?` (max one) |
| 13 | `ErrorState` | compose | Friendly failure + retry | `title?`, `description?`, `onRetry?` |
| 14 | `MoneyDisplay` | custom | **Presentation only** of a pre-computed amount | `amount` (minor units: `bigint` or integer string), `currency` (**required**), `locale?`, `signDisplay?` |
| 15 | `SkipLink` | custom | "Skip to main content" | — |

\* The shadcn `badge` file is installed only as `StatusBadge`'s implementation primitive; it is not offered as a separately-used component (use `StatusBadge`).

### A3. Non-component pieces that ship with the initial set
| Item | Notes |
|---|---|
| `lib/utils.ts` (`cn`) | generated |
| `lib/format.ts` | presentation helpers on top of `Intl` — no arithmetic |
| `lib/money.ts` | **created only when the first total/sum is needed**; integer minor-unit arithmetic; no formatting |
| `app/globals.css` token block | DESIGN_SYSTEM §2.3–2.4 |
| Route files `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx`, `not-found.tsx` | Next mechanisms, per route as needed |

## B. Removed from the previous inventory (speculative or premature)

`DataTable`, `TableToolbar`, `TableSearch`, `TableFilterSelect`, `SortableHeader`, `RowActions`, `TableSkeleton`, `TablePagination`, `LoadingState`, `InlineAlert`, `ConfirmDialog`, `StatCard`, `SummaryList`, `AmountInput`, `DateText`, `FormField`, `FormActions`, `SubmitButton`, `AppShell`, `Sidebar`/`SidebarNav`, `Topbar`, `PageContainer`, `url-state.ts`, `types/` folder, and the `/design` preview route with its demo dataset.
Replacements: the table pieces are page-local composition of `Table` + `Input` + `Select` + `Pagination`; `InlineAlert` = `Alert`; page chrome is a route layout file; `PageContainer` is a class string in the layout.
`FormField` is removed also because it collides with shadcn's `form` export.

## C. Deferred — add only when required

| Item | Add when… | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Skeleton` (shadcn) | first route with real async loading | or plain `animate-pulse` blocks in `loading.tsx` |
| `Label` (shadcn) | native `<label>` proves insufficient | |
| `Textarea`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch` | a requirement has such a field | checkbox/radio hit area ≥ 40px |
| `Dialog` / `AlertDialog` | first modal / first destructive or irreversible action | confirmation required for destructive flows |
| `Sonner` (toasts) | a justified transient-feedback need | errors never toast-only; check it for a `next-themes` import and remove it (no dark mode) |
| `Tabs`, `Tooltip`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar`, `Separator`, `Popover`/`Calendar` | a screen needs them | native `<input type="date">` first |
| `Sidebar` (shadcn) | requirements need collapsible/grouped navigation | otherwise a plain `aside` + `Sheet` |
| `form`/`field` + **React Hook Form** + `@hookform/resolvers` | real form complexity is known | optional; native form + Server Action first |
| TanStack Table | client-side multi-column sort/visibility is required | deferred |
| Advanced filtering, bulk selection | explicitly required | deferred |
| Dark mode, custom animations | explicitly required | deferred |
| Money input component | a money input exists | locale-aware parsing is **deferred until requirements** (DESIGN_SYSTEM §10.5) |
| Charts, date-range pickers, Storybook | never assumed | |

Rule: a shared component is added only with (a) a concrete requirement, (b) ≥ 2–3 call sites or a safety/accessibility reason, (c) an entry here.

## D. Dependencies

| Package | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `next`, `react`, `react-dom`, `typescript`, `tailwindcss`, `@tailwindcss/postcss` | required | stack (exact versions verified at scaffold time) |
| `lucide-react` | required | icons |
| `class-variance-authority`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `tw-animate-css`, Radix package(s) | required (installed by the shadcn CLI) | shadcn runtime; `tw-animate-css` powers built-in open/close transitions — "animations deferred" means no custom animation work |
| `zod` | **conditional** | server-side parsing of URL params and form data, introduced with the first need; a small hand-written whitelist parser is an acceptable alternative |
| `react-hook-form`, `@hookform/resolvers` | **deferred** | see §C |
| `sonner`, `next-themes` | **not installed** | `next-themes` is never needed (no dark mode) |
| Test runner (e.g. Vitest) | **not planned** | money/format logic is verified with a short script or by inspection; revisit only if a unit-test requirement appears |
| TanStack Table, date, chart, animation libraries | not installed | |

Geist comes from `next/font/google` (no package).

## E. Per-component acceptance criteria (applies to all 15)
1. Uses semantic tokens only; passes the contrast rules in DESIGN_SYSTEM §2.2.
2. Interactive parts are ≥ 40×40px (documented exceptions only) and show the §12.2 focus indicator.
3. Fully keyboard-operable; no `aria-label` on non-interactive elements; icon-only controls use `sr-only` text.
4. Accepts `className` merged via `cn()`.
5. `MoneyDisplay`: no arithmetic; currency required; exponent from `Intl`; missing value rendered with `sr-only` text.
6. Errors rendered by these components are persistent/inline (DESIGN_SYSTEM §11).

Principles:

Do not write `next lint` anywhere. `next build` also no longer runs lint, so lint is a separate step. Type checking is `npx tsc --noEmit`. Record the working commands.

|---|---|---|---|
| **0 — Approval** | Prep | This revised spec is approved; unresolved decisions listed in §4 are answered or consciously deferred | Explicit written approval |

Capture a short notes file. **Nothing is kept as deliverable code.** | All §1 items checked; spec amended if reality differed |

Phase 1 can be skipped entirely if you prefer zero prep code; in that case §1 runs at the start of Phase 2. **No phase starts without explicit approval.**

## 3. Acceptance criteria

### A. Setup (end of Phase 1 verification / Phase 2 setup)
- Versions recorded; spec reconciled with generated output.
- Lint, typecheck and build commands run successfully using the generated scripts (no `next lint`).
- `bg-success-subtle`, `text-success-subtle-foreground`, `bg-destructive-subtle`, `text-destructive-subtle-foreground`, `bg-info-subtle`, `text-muted-foreground-strong`, `border-input` all exist in built CSS; no `.dark`/`next-themes` remnants.

### B. Features

- URL parameters validated server-side with whitelists and length limits (DESIGN_SYSTEM §13.1).

- Keyboard-only pass of every screen: logical order, visible focus, no traps, skip link works, sheet/menu/dialog return focus.

# EzyFusion — UI Implementation Plan (DRAFT, awaiting review)

**Status:** specification only. No application code will be written until `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`,
`COMPONENT_INVENTORY.md` and this plan are reviewed and approved.

## 0. Isolation and safety constraints
- Prep work lives in its own directory: `~/tect-task/ezyfusion-ui-kit/` (separate from any assessment repo). Not a git repo, nothing committed, pushed or deployed.
- The assessment portal is not accessed; the assessment timer is not started.
- Only fictional sample data (e.g. "Unit 4B", "Alex Rivera", `$1,250.00`) in preview pages.
- **Hand-over strategy:** when the real assessment starts, copy (not link) these folders into the assessment repo: `src/components/{layout,data,feedback,status,finance,forms}`, `src/lib/{format,constants,url-state}.ts`, the token block from `globals.css`. Remove the `/design` preview route. No shared package, no monorepo — copying is faster and has no coupling.

## 1. Phases

| Phase | Goal | Est. | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0 – Approval** | Review the three docs, answer open questions | — | You approve |
| **1 – Scaffold & tokens** | Next 16 + TS + Tailwind + shadcn init; fonts; tokens; P0 shadcn components | 30 min | `/design` renders tokens page, no console errors |
| **2 – Layout & feedback** | AppShell, PageHeader, EmptyState/ErrorState/Skeletons, StatusBadge | 40 min | Mobile + desktop shell works; keyboard nav OK |
| **3 – Data & finance** | DataTable, pagination (URL state), Money, StatCard, forms | 60 min | Preview table with all 4 states |
| **4 – Verify & document** | a11y pass, contrast check, README of usage, "day-of checklist" | 30 min | Checklist in §5 all green |

Total prep ≈ 2.5–3 h of work, done **before** the assessment so the 4-hour window is spent on features.

## 2. Phase detail

### Phase 1 — Scaffold & tokens
1. `npx create-next-app@latest ezyfusion-ui-kit` (TypeScript, App Router, Tailwind, ESLint, `src/` dir, no Turbopack opt-out needed).
2. `npx shadcn@latest init` → accept defaults; **record the Tailwind/shadcn versions it installs** and reconcile `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §2.3` if they differ (the spec assumes Tailwind v4).
3. Replace generated colour variables with the spec tokens; delete the `.dark` block; add success/warning/danger/info extensions and `@theme inline` mappings.
4. Load Geist Sans + Geist Mono via `next/font/google`, wire `--font-geist-*`; set `<html lang="en" class="font-sans antialiased">`, `bg-background text-foreground`.
5. Add P0 shadcn components in one command.
6. Create `/design` route: token swatches, type scale, buttons, form controls (fictional).
- **Verify:** `npm run build` + `npm run lint` pass; visually compare swatches with the spec hex values; check contrast pairs from §2.2.

### Phase 2 — Layout & feedback
1. `AppShell`, `Sidebar` (static aside ≥ lg, `Sheet` < lg), `Topbar`, `PageContainer`, `PageHeader`, `SkipLink`.
2. `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `InlineAlert`, `ConfirmDialog`, `TableSkeleton`, `LoadingState`.
3. `StatusBadge` with five tones.
4. Extend `/design` with these, including all variants.
- **Verify:** resize 320 → 1440 px; keyboard-only navigation (open Sheet, close with Esc, focus returns); `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Phase 3 — Data & finance
1. `lib/format.ts` (`formatMoney` with minor units, `formatDate`) with a handful of table-driven unit checks (negative, zero, large, 0-decimal currency).
2. `Money`, `StatCard`, `SummaryList`, `AmountInput`.
3. `DataTable` shell (4 states), `TableToolbar`, `TableSearch`, `TableFilterSelect`, `TablePagination`, `RowActions`, URL-state helper.
4. `FormField`, `FormActions`, `SubmitButton` with RHF + zod example (fictional "sample record" form; no business logic).
5. `/design/table` demo with a fake in-memory dataset (≈ 57 rows) to exercise pagination, search, filter, sort, plus `?state=loading|empty|error` switches.
- **Verify:** reload preserves URL state; page resets to 1 on filter change; screen-reader names on row actions; numeric alignment; no float arithmetic on money.

### Phase 4 — Verify & document
1. Lighthouse a11y ≥ 95 on `/design`; 200 % zoom; VoiceOver pass on table + dialog.
2. Write a 1-page `README.md` in the kit: how to copy into the assessment repo, the composition rules, the component list.
3. Produce the **day-of checklist** (§5).

## 3. What will deliberately NOT be built
Dark mode · charts · date-range pickers · bulk selection · drag-and-drop · i18n/RTL framework · auth screens · any domain model (properties, tenants, leases, payments) · animations beyond spinner/pulse · Storybook (the `/design` route is the living style guide — zero extra tooling).

## 4. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Installed shadcn/Tailwind versions differ from spec | Phase 1 step 2 reconciliation; tokens are version-agnostic |
| Requirements need client-side table features | Escape hatch: swap `DataTable` internals for TanStack, keep its props |
| Currency/locale unknown | Config constants + `Intl`; no symbols hard-coded |
| Prep over-engineering | Hard timebox per phase; P1/P2 only when needed |
| Design kit leaks into assessment as dead code | Copy only used components; delete `/design` |
| Brand colours fail AA | Derived foreground tokens (spec §2.2) |

## 5. Day-of checklist (once the assessment starts — not now)
1. Scaffold the assessment app; run `shadcn init` and record versions.
2. Paste token block + `format.ts` + constants; copy required component folders.
3. Add only the shadcn components the first screens need.
4. Build pages as `PageContainer > PageHeader > Card(s)`; map domain statuses → `StatusBadge` tones in a local 5-line map.
5. Every list gets the 4 states; every mutation gets toast + error path.
6. Final 15 minutes: keyboard pass, mobile pass, remove unused components, `build` + `lint`.

## 6. Approval requested
Please confirm or amend:
1. Token approach incl. derived AA foreground tokens (DESIGN_SYSTEM §2.2).
2. No dark mode.
3. Placeholder currency/locale for previews (`USD`, `en-US`).
4. `react-hook-form` + `zod` allowed as the only extra runtime deps.
5. `DataTable` as a thin shell over shadcn `Table` (no TanStack).
6. Kit location `~/tect-task/ezyfusion-ui-kit/` and the copy-not-link hand-over.

On approval I will start Phase 1 only; I will pause for review after each phase if you prefer.

All three documents in `/Users/youssefkhaled/tect-task` are updated to v0.2 with your amendments. I haven't implemented anything: no components, no installs, no commit, push or deploy, and I didn't touch the portal. The contrast figures come from a Node script I ran, not from a browser check.

## 1. Summary of changes per file

**[DESIGN_SYSTEM.md](DESIGN_SYSTEM.md)** (rewritten)
- **Accessibility:**
  - The input border is now `--input: #7C8BA1`. It measures 3.46:1 on white, 3.23:1 on the page background and 3.08:1 on the `#EEF2F8` tint. The old value was 1.48:1.
  - `--muted-foreground-strong: #526077` is a new token. The brand `#64748B` is kept for white surfaces only. Page background, tinted fills and table rows use the strong token.
  - `text-destructive` is allowed on white only. On other surfaces use `#991B1B`.
  - Interactive targets are 40px minimum as a house rule. The `sm` button size is removed. A table lists WCAG 2.5.8 (AA, 24px) and 2.5.5 (AAA, 44px) alongside it.
  - Focus is a solid 2px primary ring with a 2px offset. shadcn's default `ring-ring/50` is about 2.6:1, which fails the 3:1 rule, so the generated focus classes get replaced. I also added keyboard rules and the WCAG 2.2 criteria that apply.
  - Important errors now stay inline until fixed. This replaces my earlier "≤ 4s toast". Success messages must last at least 6s and pause on hover or focus.
  - `aria-label` is no longer used on non-interactive elements. Visible text or `sr-only` text is used instead.
- **Tokens:**
  - `destructive` is used everywhere. The word `danger` appears only as the palette label in the brand table.
  - Extension tokens are exactly 11 (3 success, 3 warning, 2 destructive tints, 2 info, 1 strong muted).
  - Naming follows shadcn's pattern: `X-foreground` is text on the solid colour, `X-subtle-foreground` is text on the tint.
  - Tailwind v4 rules added: register every token under `--color-*` or no utility is generated, restore the default border colour, and remove `.dark` and `next-themes`.
- **Components:** the `FormField` clash is resolved by dropping that wrapper. There is no `DataTable`. React Hook Form is deferred. TanStack Table, advanced filtering, animation work and dark mode are deferred.
- **Money:**
  - Arithmetic and presentation are separate.
  - The currency is a required prop.
  - The minor-unit exponent comes from `Intl`, never a hard-coded `100`.
  - Conversion uses decimal-string manipulation, not float division.
  - The limits of JavaScript `number` (`MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) are documented.
  - API parsing and rounding rules are deferred.
- **Security:** a new §13 covers server-side validation of URL parameters, whitelists for sort fields and page sizes, a 64-character search limit, no sensitive data in URLs, server-side authorization on every mutation, never trusting client totals, and server-enforced payment idempotency.

**[COMPONENT_INVENTORY.md](COMPONENT_INVENTORY.md)** (rewritten)
- It now lists exactly 15 components, with the removed items and the triggers for each deferred one.
- Dependencies are revised, and per-component acceptance criteria are added.

**[UI_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](UI_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md)** (rewritten)
- Preparation and assessment work are separated into two tracks. No prebuilt code is assumed reusable.
- The preview route, demo dataset and kit README are gone.
- A version-verification section is added, and acceptance criteria A, B and C.
- The lint command is covered: don't use `next lint`, use the script that `create-next-app` generates for Next 16 (expected to call `eslint`, to be confirmed), and run `tsc --noEmit` separately.

## 2. Updated component inventory (15)

| Group | Components |
|---|---|
| shadcn primitives (9) | Button, Input, Select, Card, Table, Pagination, Alert, Sheet, DropdownMenu |
| Shared (6) | StatusBadge, PageHeader, EmptyState, ErrorState, MoneyDisplay, SkipLink |

StatusBadge uses shadcn's `badge` file as its implementation, and that file is installed with it. Everything else is deferred until a requirement needs it.

## 3. Updated implementation phases

| Phase | Track | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Prep | Approval of this spec and the unresolved decisions |
| 1 | Prep, optional | Scaffold in a throwaway folder outside any assessment repo and record the real versions. Confirm the lint, typecheck and build commands. Confirm the tokens and the focus and size classes match the spec. Keep nothing as a deliverable. |
| 2 | Assessment | After the requirements and rules are read: scaffold, `shadcn init`, tokens, fonts, the two allowed edits |
| 3 | Assessment | Build features with the 15 components, adding deferred items only on demand |
| 4 | Assessment | Keyboard and accessibility pass, security checklist, remove unused code, run lint, typecheck and build |

## 4. Remaining unresolved decisions

1. Whether any prepared files or snippets may be used in the submission (needs the assessment rules).
2. Whether Phase 1 runs at all, and where the sandbox lives (I proposed `~/ezyfusion-prep-sandbox/`).
3. Currency, locale, API money format and rounding (needs requirements).
4. `zod` or a hand-written parameter parser.
5. React Hook Form (deferred until form complexity is known).
6. Whether search terms stay in the URL, given personal-name privacy (needs requirements).
7. Whether navigation exists (needs requirements).
8. The authentication and authorization model, and what idempotency support the backend has.
9. Negative amount style (`signDisplay` or accounting).

## 5. Contradictions still present

- **Dismissing errors:** the error rule says errors persist until fixed or "explicitly dismissed". shadcn's `Alert` has no dismiss control, so either dismissal is dropped or a button is added.
- **Allowed edits:** I limited edits to generated shadcn files to "size variants" and focus classes. The 40px rule also touches `Select` item heights and `Pagination` sizes. I count these as size edits, but the wording is loose.
- **Skip link target:** the `SkipLink` is in the root layout, but `<main id="main">` sits in the `(app)` layout. Pages outside that group, such as `not-found`, would have no target.
- **Version-dependent claims:** these are hedged in the docs and need checking against the installed versions:
  - `destructive-foreground` may or may not be generated.
  - `proxy.ts` replacing `middleware.ts`.
  - `searchParams` being a Promise.
  - `next lint` having been removed.
  - Exact string support in `Intl.NumberFormat`.

## 6. Confirmation

Only these three Markdown files exist in the folder. The one script I ran was a read-only contrast calculation. Phase 1 has not started.

I'm waiting for your approval and your call on Phase 1 before doing anything else.

title: proxy.js
description: API reference for the proxy.js file.
related:
  title: Learn more about Proxy
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-request
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-response
---

> **Note**: The `middleware` file convention is deprecated and has been renamed to `proxy`. See [Migration to Proxy](#migration-to-proxy) for more details.

The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

Proxy executes before routes are rendered. It's particularly useful for implementing custom server-side logic like authentication, logging, or handling redirects.

> **Good to know**:
>
> Proxy is meant to be invoked separately of your render code and in optimized cases deployed to your CDN for fast redirect/rewrite handling, you should not attempt relying on shared modules or globals.
>
> To pass information from Proxy to your application, use [headers](#setting-headers), [cookies](#using-cookies), [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#rewrite), [redirects](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#redirect), or the URL.

Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.

If you’ve customized [`pageExtensions`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions), for example to `.page.ts` or `.page.js`, name your file `proxy.page.ts` or `proxy.page.js` accordingly.

```tsx filename="proxy.ts" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

title: cacheComponents
description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
related:
  links:
    - app/getting-started/caching
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
---

Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.

## Usage

To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file, together with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching):

```ts filename="next.config.ts"
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

Set `partialPrefetching` explicitly. Leaving it unset logs a warning, because the first release of Cache Components did not include Partial Prefetching. Set it to `false` only while [migrating an app that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.

Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.

## Usage

To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file, together with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching):

```ts filename="next.config.ts"
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

Set `partialPrefetching` explicitly. Leaving it unset logs a warning, because the first release of Cache Components did not include Partial Prefetching. Set it to `false` only while [migrating an app that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.

content.text:
## 1. Files created

All files are in `~/ezyfusion-prep-sandbox/app/`. The scaffold's own config, lockfile and `public/` assets are omitted.

**Hand-written**
- `src/app/globals.css` — tokens, `@theme inline` mapping, base rules
- `src/app/layout.tsx` — fonts, `SkipLink`, `AppShell`
- `src/app/page.tsx` — demo dashboard
- `src/app/_components/demo-data.ts` — fictional invoices and status-to-tone map
- `src/app/_components/invoices-table.tsx` — table, search, status filter, pagination, empty state
- `src/app/_components/new-invoice-form.tsx` — demo form with inline errors
- `src/app/_components/states-demo.tsx` — empty and error state demo
- `src/components/app-shell.tsx` — sidebar from `lg`, header, mobile `Sheet` drawer, `<main id="main">`
- `src/components/skip-link.tsx`, `page-header.tsx`, `status-badge.tsx`, `empty-state.tsx`, `error-state.tsx`, `money-display.tsx`
- `src/lib/format.ts` — `Intl` presentation only
- `src/lib/money.ts` — `bigint` arithmetic only
- `tsconfig.json` — target raised from ES2017 to ES2020 so `bigint` is allowed

**shadcn-generated, then edited** (in `src/components/ui/`): `button`, `input`, `select`, `card`, `table`, `pagination`, `alert`, `sheet`, `dropdown-menu`, `badge` (installed only as `StatusBadge`'s base), plus `src/lib/utils.ts`.

The edits to the generated files were:
- Button and Input are `h-10`, and the `sm`/`xs` button sizes are removed.
- Select trigger and items are 40px.
- Menu items are `min-h-10`, and the pagination ellipsis is `size-10`.
- Every `dark:` class is stripped.
- Focus is now a solid 2px outline in the primary colour with a 2px offset, replacing shadcn's translucent ring.
- The destructive button is solid red.
- `Alert` gains a `success` variant and tinted destructive colours.
- `Alert` role is `alert` for destructive and `status` otherwise.

## 2. Packages installed and versions

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| next | 16.4.2 |
| react / react-dom | 19.3.0 |
| typescript | 5.9.3 |
| tailwindcss | 4.3.3 |
| @tailwindcss/turbopack | 4.3.3 |
| eslint / eslint-config-next | 9.39.5 / 16.4.2 |
| shadcn (CLI, also a runtime dependency) | 4.22.1 |
| @base-ui/react | 1.9.0 |
| class-variance-authority | 0.7.1 |
| cn (replaces clsx and tailwind-merge) | 0.5.0 |
| lucide-react | 1.60.0 |
| tw-animate-css | 1.4.0 |

Node is v24.21.0 and npm is 11.19.0. `next-themes` and `sonner` are not installed.

## 3. Validation results

- **Lint:** `npm run lint` (which runs `eslint`) passes with no output. The installed docs confirm `next lint` was removed in Next 16.
- **Typecheck:** `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- **Build:** `npm run build` passes. `/` and `/_not-found` are both statically prerendered.
- **Tokens:** all 10 custom token utilities I checked (success, warning, destructive and info tints and their text colours, `muted-foreground-strong`, `border-input`) exist in the built CSS. There are no `prefers-color-scheme` rules and no `next-themes`.
- **Next 16 APIs checked in the installed docs:**
  - `proxy.ts` replaces `middleware`.
  - `searchParams` is a Promise.
  - `cacheComponents` and `partialPrefetching` are enabled by the scaffold.
- **Keyboard:**
  - The skip link is the first tab stop and becomes visible.
  - Enter on it focuses `main#main`.
  - The next Tab goes to "Create invoice".
  - The focus indicator measured 2px solid `#1E40AF` with a 2px offset.
  - The tab order across the 25 focusable elements is logical.
- **Targets:** every interactive element measured 40px or more on both desktop and mobile, including Select, Pagination and menu items.
- **Responsive, 375px:**
  - There is no horizontal page scroll, and the table scrolls inside its card.
  - The sidebar is hidden and the drawer works: it is labelled, focus moves inside, Esc closes it, and focus returns to the trigger.
  - Pagination collapses to "Page 1 of 3".
- **Form:**
  - Empty submit shows a persistent destructive summary alert and per-field errors, and focus moves to the first invalid field.
  - A value with too many decimals (12.345) is rejected rather than rounded.
  - A valid amount parses to $1,250.50.
  - The alert disappears once the fields are fixed. It has no dismiss control.

## 4. Remaining issues

1. **The spec assumed Radix, but shadcn 4.22.1's default style is Base UI.** The scaffold also uses `@tailwindcss/turbopack` rather than the PostCSS plugin. `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` and `COMPONENT_INVENTORY.md` need amending.
2. **shadcn's generated `destructive` button, badge and alert were tinted.** I changed them to match the spec, so these edits go beyond the "size and focus only" rule. The spec's allowed-edits wording needs updating.
3. **`transition-all` animates the focus outline.** Read straight after focusing, it shows a transient 3px white outline. It settles to 2px blue.
4. **Demo shortcuts.** Pagination, search and filter state are local React state, not URL parameters. The sidebar "Invoices" and "New invoice" items are in-page anchors, and the row-menu "View details" item is disabled.
5. **Not tested.**
   - Zero- and three-decimal currencies were not exercised, because the demo is USD only.
   - No screen reader was used, and no Lighthouse run.
   - Select keyboard behaviour was only lightly checked. Space opens it, but I did not step through its options.
6. **Dependency audit.** `npm install` reported 5 high-severity vulnerabilities. I did not investigate them.
7. **Leftover scaffold files.** The default `public/*.svg` files and `README.md` remain.

## 5. Command to run the demo

```bash
cd ~/ezyfusion-prep-sandbox/app && npm run dev
```

Then open http://localhost:3000. For a production run, use `npm run build && npm run start`.

content.text:
# Cycle 1.1 report

## Result

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| ESLint (`npm run lint`) | **PASS** |
| Typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) | **PASS** |
| Production build | **PASS** (`/` and `/_not-found` static) |
| Money tests (`npm test`) | **PASS**, 22 of 22 |
| `transition-all` focus check | **PASS**, fixed |
| `npm audit` | **9 high findings remain**, 0 in the production dependency set |

## 1. Security findings

`npm audit --json` reports **9** high findings, not 5. The "5" in the install output was the earlier scaffold's count. All 9 come from **one advisory**: [GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm), a stack-exhaustion denial of service in `braces` (versions up to 3.0.3, CVSS 7.5).

**Dependency chains** (the first three rows are the 9 findings, with `micromatch` and `fast-glob` shared between paths):

| Path | Findings |
|---|---|
| `braces@3.0.3` → `micromatch@4.0.8` → `fast-glob` | `braces`, `micromatch`, `fast-glob` |
| `shadcn` → `@shadcn/registry` / `fast-glob` / `ts-morph` → `@ts-morph/common` → `fast-glob` | `shadcn`, `@shadcn/registry`, `ts-morph`, `@ts-morph/common` |
| `eslint-config-next` → `@next/eslint-plugin-next` → `fast-glob` | `eslint-config-next`, `@next/eslint-plugin-next` |

**Available fix:** none. `braces` 3.0.3 is the latest release on npm, so no patched version exists. npm's suggested "fixes" are `shadcn@1.0.0` and `eslint-config-next@14.2.35`. Both are downgrades, so I did not apply them. I ran no `--force` command.

**Runtime impact:** none for the running app. The advisory needs an attacker-controlled glob pattern. The affected tools (the shadcn CLI, ESLint and ts-morph) only run at build or lint time on fixed patterns, and none is loaded by `next start`.

**One change I made:** `shadcn` was under `dependencies` only because `globals.css` imports `shadcn/tailwind.css`. I moved it to `devDependencies`. `npm audit --omit=dev` went from 7 findings to **0**, and the build still passes.

## 2. Tests executed

They are `src/lib/money.test.ts` and `src/lib/format.test.ts`. They use Node's built-in `node:test`, so there are no new dependencies. Run them with `npm test`.

- **USD, JPY, KWD:** currency precision is 2, 0 and 3 decimals, and formatted output is `$1,250.00`, `¥1,250` and `KWD 1,250.500`.
- **Zero and negatives:** zero formats correctly, and negative amounts show a sign (`-$45.00`).
- **Large amounts:**
  - `9007199254740993` minor units (past `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) formats as `$90,071,992,547,409.93`.
  - A 30-digit value also formats exactly.
  - Sums stay exact, and a test confirms a JS `number` cannot hold the same value.
- **Invalid precision:** `12.345` for USD, `12.5` for JPY and `1.2345` for KWD return `null`. Nothing is rounded.
- **Malformed input:** 15 cases return `null`: empty, `abc`, `1,250.00`, `-5`, `+5`, `.5`, `5.`, `1e3`, `1.2.3`, `NaN`, non-ASCII digits and others.
- **Other:** an invalid currency code throws `RangeError`, and date formatting shows no timezone shift.

**Supporting changes:** I added `allowImportingTsExtensions` to `tsconfig.json` so the tests can import `.ts` files, and a `test` script to `package.json`. The test script uses `--no-warnings` to silence a harmless Node module-type warning.

## 3. `transition-all` and focus visibility

`transition-all` animated the outline, so right after focusing, the ring showed as a transient 3px white outline at 0 offset before settling to 2px blue. The ring was never absent, but the first frames were wrong. It also ignored reduced-motion preferences.

I replaced it in `button.tsx` and `badge.tsx` with `transition-[color,background-color,border-color,transform] motion-reduce:transition-none`. Computed styles now show button, icon button and pagination link transitions no longer include any outline property.

`Input` and `Select` use `transition-colors`, which animates only `outline-color`. Their ring appears at full size immediately and fades colour for 0.15s, and both colours stay at least 3:1 on white. I left them alone.

## Remaining blockers

- **`braces` findings:** nothing to do until a patched `braces` is published. Re-run `npm audit` later.
- **Frame-accurate focus capture:** I couldn't capture the first rendered frame of a real keyboard focus with the available tooling. The outline fix rests on the computed transition properties above, plus the earlier check that the settled ring is 2px solid `#1E40AF` with a 2px offset.

content.text:
# shadcn/ui verification report

This was read-only. I fetched the registry originals with the local CLI's `view` command (nothing installed or written to the project) and compared them with the files in `~/ezyfusion-prep-sandbox/app`.

## 1. Official shadcn/ui?

**Yes.** The components were generated by the official CLI (`shadcn@4.22.1`) from the registry's `base-nova` style. `components.json` records that style, and `table.tsx` is byte-identical to the registry original. The other files differ only by the style transform the CLI applies on install and by my edits (section 6). I verified this against registry output, not against the shadcn source repo.

The `cn` package that `src/lib/utils.ts` re-exports is the shadcn team's utility, replacing `clsx` and `tailwind-merge`. Its `package.json` points at `github.com/shadcn-ui/cn`. I only checked that metadata, not the package's provenance.

## 2. Installed components

All 10 files are in `src/components/ui/`, plus `src/lib/utils.ts`.

| File | Used as |
|---|---|
| `button.tsx` | Button |
| `input.tsx` | Input |
| `select.tsx` | Select |
| `card.tsx` | Card |
| `table.tsx` | Table |
| `pagination.tsx` | Pagination |
| `alert.tsx` | Alert |
| `sheet.tsx` | Sheet (mobile drawer) |
| `dropdown-menu.tsx` | DropdownMenu |
| `badge.tsx` | Base for `StatusBadge` only |

## 3. Base UI or Radix?

**Base UI.** The imports are `@base-ui/react/{button,input,select,menu,dialog,use-render,merge-props}`. There is no Radix import and no Radix package in `package.json`. The approved spec assumed Radix, so it is wrong on this point.

## 4. Custom components that duplicate shadcn

Checked against the registry with `shadcn view`:

| Our code | shadcn equivalent | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Inline `Field` (page-local in `new-invoice-form.tsx`) | `field` | Overlaps. Deliberately deferred. |
| Native `<label>` elements | `label` | Overlaps. Deliberately deferred. |
| `EmptyState` | `empty` | Overlaps. Written before I confirmed `empty` exists. |
| `ErrorState` | `empty` (partly) | Same. |
| `StatusBadge` | wraps `badge` | Not a duplicate. |
| `AppShell` | `sidebar` | Deliberately avoided (see the spec's trade-off). |
| `PageHeader`, `SkipLink`, `MoneyDisplay` | none | Fine. |

## 5. Tailwind v4 and design-system configuration

- **Tailwind v4:** correct.
  - There is no `tailwind.config` or `postcss.config`, and `components.json` has an empty `tailwind.config`.
  - The CSS is `@import "tailwindcss"`, `tw-animate-css`, `shadcn/tailwind.css` and `@theme inline`. `shadcn/tailwind.css` supplies the `data-open` and `data-closed` variants the components use.
  - The scaffold wires Tailwind through `@tailwindcss/turbopack` rather than PostCSS. That works with the Next 16.4.2 scaffold.
- **Tokens:** all brand tokens plus the 11 extension tokens are defined in `:root` and registered under `--color-*`.
  - Earlier I confirmed the built CSS contains the custom utilities.
  - There is no `.dark` block and no `@custom-variant dark`.
- **Not applied:** the generated components use the shadcn radius scale. I overrode `--radius` and `--radius-*` in the theme, so the 8px and 10px values are mine.

## 6. Modifications to the generated files

I made all of these myself.

| Edit | Files | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 40px sizes (`h-10`, `size-10`, `min-h-10`) and `sm` variants removed | button, input, select, dropdown-menu, pagination, sheet | **Needed.** The spec requires 40px. |
| Focus changed from a translucent ring to a solid 2px outline | button, input, select, badge, menu items | **Justified for Button and Badge.** On Input and Select the generated `focus-visible:border-ring` also changes the border to solid primary, so the old indicator was arguably already adequate. |
| All `dark:` classes stripped | all files | **Debatable.** Without the dark variant, Tailwind v4 maps `dark:` to `prefers-color-scheme`. I stripped the classes. One line (`@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))`) would have made them inert and kept the files closer to upstream. |
| `bg-transparent` → `bg-card` on Input and Select | input, select | **Unnecessary.** Cosmetic, not required by any accessibility rule. |
| Solid destructive button, `border-input` on the outline variant | button | **Spec-driven.** The upstream destructive style is a tint. |
| New `success` and tinted destructive variants, padding, role logic | alert | **Partly avoidable.** The role could be set at call sites instead of editing the component. |
| `transition-all` replaced with targeted transitions | button, badge | **Needed.** Fixes the focus-outline animation. |
| `cn-font-heading` → `font-heading` in `CardTitle` | card | **Not my edit.** The CLI applied it when generating the file. |

## Recommendations

1. **Amend the spec**, since it says Radix: the system is Base UI with `base-nova`. Edits to generated files are also wider than the two types the spec allows.
2. **Revert the `dark:` stripping** and restore the one-line custom variant (optional, to track upstream more closely). Otherwise keep it and note it.
3. **Revert `bg-card` on Input and Select**, or confirm you want it.
4. **Before adding more form UI,** decide whether to adopt shadcn's `field`, `label` and `empty` instead of the custom versions. They're one `shadcn add` away, but adding them means a fix to the page-local `Field` and to `EmptyState`/`ErrorState`.
5. **Keep a note of the small set of intentional edits** (sizes, focus, destructive button, alert variants) so they can be re-applied if shadcn files are regenerated.

Implement the following UI improvements in one focused cycle.
Do not create new specification documents or refactor unrelated code.
1. Modern Focus States
Review every interactive form component:

* Input
* Select
* DatePicker
* DropdownMenu triggers
* Buttons

Replace visually aggressive focus styling with a modern, subtle and consistent design.
Requirements:

* Keep a clearly visible keyboard focus indicator.
* Avoid double borders, heavy shadows and oversized rings.
* Use consistent focus-visible behavior.
* Preserve WCAG accessibility requirements.
* Ensure mouse interaction does not produce unnecessary keyboard-style focus rings.
* Support reduced motion preferences.

Do not remove keyboard focus accessibility.
2. Advanced Dropdown UX
Use the official shadcn/ui components compatible with the existing Base UI and base-nova setup.
Improve Select and DropdownMenu:

* Consistent trigger design.
* Proper spacing and typography.
* Clear hover and selected states.
* Keyboard navigation.
* Escape to close.
* Correct focus restoration.
* Appropriate menu max-height and internal scrolling.
* Proper viewport collision handling.
* Correct layering and z-index.
* Avoid unnecessary custom dropdown implementations.

Do not introduce Radix UI or replace the existing Base UI foundation.
3. DatePicker
Install the official shadcn/ui Calendar and Popover components, using the versions compatible with the current project.
Create a reusable DatePicker component with:

* Calendar popover.
* Consistent trigger appearance.
* Clear date formatting.
* Placeholder.
* Disabled state.
* Optional minimum and maximum dates.
* Keyboard accessibility.
* Correct popover positioning.
* No date timezone shifting.
* Clear selection only when enabled.

  modal?: boolean | undefined;

  actionsRef?: React.RefObject<PopoverRoot.Actions | null> | undefined;
  /**
   * Determines if the popover enters a modal state when open.
   * - `true`: user interaction is limited to the popover: document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.

   * - `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the popover, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled.

   * When `modal` is `true`, focus trapping is enabled only if `<Popover.Close>` is rendered

   *
   * When `modal` is `'trap-focus'`, render `<Popover.Close>` inside `<Popover.Popup>` so touch

# Cycle 1.2 report

## 1. Files modified or created

All files are under `~/ezyfusion-prep-sandbox/app`.

**Created**
- `src/components/date-picker.tsx`: reusable DatePicker
- `src/lib/date.ts`: date-only parse and format helpers
- `src/lib/date.test.ts`: 5 new tests
- `src/components/ui/calendar.tsx` and `popover.tsx`: official shadcn files, added via the CLI

**Modified**
- `src/app/globals.css`: new `focus-ring` and `field-control` utilities and a reduced-motion block
- `src/components/ui/`:
  - `button.tsx` and `badge.tsx` use the shared focus style.
  - `input.tsx`, `select.tsx` and `dropdown-menu.tsx` use `field-control`, non-modal defaults and collision handling.
  - `calendar.tsx` has two fixes: the missing `ref` and the duplicate focus ring.
- `src/app/_components/new-invoice-form.tsx`: the native date input is now the DatePicker, the three fields share one row, and each field reserves a line for its error.
- `package.json`: adds `react-day-picker` 10.0.2 and `date-fns` 4.4.0 (installed by the Calendar component).

## 2. UI improvements

- **Focus:** two styles, both `:focus-visible` only.
  - Buttons, links, icon buttons and calendar days get a solid 2px primary outline with a 2px offset.
  - Input, Select and DatePicker get one border that turns primary, plus a soft 2px halo at 30% opacity. There is no box-shadow and no second border.
  - A mouse click on a button shows no ring, and Tab shows it. Reduced motion is honoured by an unlayered rule, with no `!important`.
- **Fields:** Input, Select trigger and DatePicker trigger now share `field-control`. All three are 40px tall and fill their container. They use the same radius, border, 16px text on mobile and 14px from `md`, and the same hover, invalid and disabled states.
- **Select:**
  - It opens below the trigger instead of overlapping it.
  - The popup width matches the trigger, and its height is capped at `min(available height, 20rem)` with internal scrolling.
  - Items have a highlight state and a selected state (bold plus check).
  - `collisionPadding` is 8px.
  - The default is non-modal.
- **DropdownMenu:** same non-modal default and collision padding. Items are 40px, and the menu has a 160px minimum width and the same height cap.
- **Form layout:** each field's error line reserves a fixed height, so validation messages no longer shift the layout.

## 3. Root cause of page scroll locking

Base UI's `Select` and `Menu` default to `modal={true}`. Its own docs say that means "document page scroll is locked and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled." Our code used the generated wrappers unchanged, so every ordinary dropdown behaved like a modal.

The fix is in the wrappers: `Select` and `DropdownMenu` now default to `modal={false}`. It is not a CSS override, and there are no changes to `body` overflow or `pointer-events`. Popover is already non-modal by default.

The mobile Sheet drawer keeps its lock. With the drawer open, `<body>` gets `overflow: hidden`, focus stays inside, and Escape closes it.

## 4. DatePicker details

- **Interface:** `value` and `onChange` use `YYYY-MM-DD`, with an empty string for no selection. Other props are `min`, `max`, `placeholder`, `disabled`, `clearable`, `name`, `id` and the ARIA props.
- **No timezone shift:** a `Date` is built from local year, month and day, and read back with the local getters. `parseIsoDate` rejects non-existent dates such as 2026-02-30. The display text uses the existing UTC-pinned `formatDate`. Tests cover round-trips across UTC-11 to UTC+14 and leap days.
- **Calendar:** shadcn `Calendar` in a non-modal `Popover`, with 40px day cells and a 304px popup.
  - Selection is required, so clicking the selected day does not clear it.
  - Month navigation stops at `min` and `max` (verified as January 2026 to December 2027 in the demo).
  - It opens on the selected month, or today's month clamped into the range.
- **Focus:** opening lands on the selected day, else today, else the first enabled day. Selecting a date, or pressing Escape, returns focus to the trigger.
- **Clear:** a sibling button (not nested in the trigger), 40px, shown only when `clearable`, a date is selected and the picker is enabled.

**Fix to the generated `Calendar`:** the registry's `CalendarDayButton` created a `ref` but never attached it. As a result, arrow keys moved react-day-picker's internal focus but not the browser focus. I added `ref={ref}`.

## 5. Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run lint` | **PASS** |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | **PASS** |
| `npm test` | **PASS**, 27 of 27 (22 money and format, 5 date) |
| `npm run build` | **PASS** (`/` and `/_not-found` static) |
| Production `npm audit --omit=dev` | 0 vulnerabilities |
| Page scrolls with Select and menu open | **PASS** (desktop and 375px) |
| Long dropdown internal scroll | **PASS** (118px cap in a 300px viewport; End key scrolls the list, page stays put) |
| Arrow-key option navigation, Escape, focus restoration (Select, menu) | **PASS** |
| DatePicker open, keyboard select, Escape, clear | **PASS** (Oct 20 + 3 right + 1 down = Oct 30, value shown as "Oct 30, 2026") |
| Field dimensions, desktop and mobile | **PASS** (all 40px, same radius, border and font; 311px wide at 375px) |
| Mouse versus keyboard focus ring | **PASS** |
| Sheet scroll lock and focus trap | **PASS** |

## 6. Remaining issues

- **Focus restoration is delayed.** After a menu, Select or popover closes, focus returns to the trigger about 400ms later, not instantly. At 100ms it was still elsewhere. This is Base UI's close handling.
- **Untested:**
  - The DatePicker `disabled` state is not exercised in the demo; I checked the code only.
  - The reduced-motion rule was reviewed but not run with the OS preference on.
  - Wheel and touch scrolling inside a long dropdown was not tested (keyboard and layout were).
  - No screen reader was used.
- **Direct edits to generated files.** The `calendar.tsx` ref fix and the other changes to `select.tsx`, `dropdown-menu.tsx` and `input.tsx` mean these files will need re-applying if shadcn files are regenerated.
- **Moved off the demo path.** Opening the popup while it is still fading in can make size measurements read about 5% small. Final sizes were checked after the animation finished.
- **Dependency audit.** The 9 high findings from before are unchanged, with 0 in the production dependency set.

EzyFusion — Cycle 2: Local Infrastructure Setup & Validation
Act as a Senior Backend Engineer and DevOps Engineer.
We are preparing for a timed 4-hour technical assessment for EzyFusion Group.
The assessment requires:

* Next.js 16 with TypeScript
* Local Supabase using Docker and Supabase CLI
* PostgreSQL
* Supabase Auth, RLS and Storage
* Prisma ORM
* Reproducible database migrations and seed scripts

The assessment has NOT started.
Your responsibility is to prepare, implement and validate the local infrastructure in a disposable sandbox.
Workspace
Use:
~/ezyfusion-infra-sandbox/
Do not modify:

* ~/tect-task/
* ~/ezyfusion-prep-sandbox/
* Existing unrelated projects, containers or Docker volumes.

Phase A — Environment & Supabase

1. Inspect Node.js, npm, Git, Docker and Supabase CLI versions.
2. Verify Docker Desktop is running and has sufficient resources.
3. Check available disk space and local port conflicts.
4. Initialize Supabase locally.
5. Start the Supabase stack and allow required images to download.
6. Verify:
   * PostgreSQL connectivity
   * Supabase Studio
   * Auth service
   * Storage service
   * Local API gateway
7. Record local service URLs and non-secret configuration.

If Docker or Supabase fails, investigate and fix only sandbox-specific problems.
Phase B — Prisma & Database

1. Initialize a minimal TypeScript project with a compatible Prisma version.
2. Configure Prisma to connect to local Supabase PostgreSQL.
3. Verify database connectivity.
4. Create a disposable sample model unrelated to the assessment.
5. Choose and document one authoritative migration workflow.
6. Test migration creation and application.
7. Create a deterministic seed script.
8. Verify database reset and clean reconstruction.

Avoid conflicting Prisma and Supabase migration histories.
Do not create actual leases, invoices or payment tables.
Phase C — RLS & Security
Create a minimal disposable security experiment.

1. Create two test users.
2. Create a simple tenant-owned sample table.
3. Enable RLS.
4. Create policies enforcing ownership.
5. Verify User A cannot read or modify User B's records.
6. Verify unauthenticated access is denied.
7. Verify the actual Prisma connection's RLS behavior.
8. Explain any RLS bypass by privileged database roles.
9. Demonstrate the server-side authorization boundary.

Use local credentials only. Never expose database credentials or service-role keys to the browser.
Phase D — Validation
Execute real checks for:

* Supabase stack health
* PostgreSQL connectivity
* Auth and Storage availability
* Prisma queries
* Migration reproducibility
* Seed reproducibility
* Database reset
* RLS isolation
* No modifications to unrelated infrastructure

Do not claim PASS for checks that were not executed.
Constraints

* Do not access the assessment portal.
* Do not start the timer.
* Do not implement assessment features.
* Do not commit, push or deploy.
* Do not prune unrelated Docker resources.
* Do not modify global machine settings without permission.
* Do not create unnecessary documentation.
* Keep all experiments disposable and isolated.

Final Report
Provide:

1. Environment versions and health.
2. Supabase services and URLs.
3. Prisma connection and migration results.
4. Seed and reset results.
5. RLS tests and security findings.
6. Exact reproduction commands.
7. Remaining blockers.
8. GO / NO-GO readiness decision.

Stop after completing Cycle 2.
</pasted_content id="a84f">

content.text:
# Cycle 2 report: local infrastructure

**Decision: GO.** Every check below was run, and the failures I hit are listed under blockers. Two items are not verified (see section 8).

## 1. Environment versions and health

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Node / npm / Git | v24.21.0 / 11.19.0 / 2.54.0 |
| Docker | 29.7.2, Compose v5.5.1, 10 CPUs, 8.3 GB memory |
| Supabase CLI | 2.121.0, installed locally in the project (not globally) |
| Prisma | 7.10.1 (stable) |
| Disk | 232 GB free |
| Ports | Supabase's ports were free. Host Postgres on 5432 and something on 3000 belong to you and were left alone. |

**Docker Desktop was not running, so I launched it.** It came up in about 10 seconds. Two of your existing Postgres containers (`coach-omar-recipe-book-db-1`, `edfa3ly-postgres`) restarted with it because of their restart policy. I did not touch them, and their volumes are unchanged.

I pinned Prisma to 7.10.1. The npm `latest` tag currently points at `8.0.0-rc.23`.

## 2. Supabase services and URLs

I disabled analytics and the edge runtime in `supabase/config.toml` to save memory. Nine containers run, all healthy.

| Service | URL | Result |
|---|---|---|
| API gateway | `http://127.0.0.1:54321` | reachable |
| Auth | `/auth/v1/health` | 200, GoTrue v2.197.0 |
| Storage | `/storage/v1/status` | 200; bucket list with the service key also 200 |
| REST | `/rest/v1/` | 200 |
| Studio | `http://127.0.0.1:54323` | 307 redirect (reachable) |
| Mail (Mailpit) | `http://127.0.0.1:54324` | 200 |
| PostgreSQL | `postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres` | connected, PostgreSQL 17.11 |

Keys are in `.env` only (mode 600, git-ignored). I never printed them.

## 3. Prisma connection and migration results

- **Prisma connects** via the pg driver adapter, and `prisma generate` works.
- **Migration workflow decision: Prisma Migrate is the single authoritative history.** `supabase/migrations/` stays empty on purpose. The Supabase CLI only runs the stack and `supabase db reset`. This is also written at the top of `prisma.config.ts`.
- **Migration:** `20261020192950_init_sandbox_notes` creates the `sandbox_notes` table, enables RLS, adds four ownership policies, and sets the grants.
- **`migrate dev` works.** It replays migrations on a persistent shadow database (`ezy_shadow`) with minimal stand-ins for `auth.users` and `auth.uid()`. `scripts/prepare-shadow-db.ts` creates it.
- **After applying:** `prisma migrate status` reports up to date, and `prisma migrate diff` shows no difference.
- **Trade-off:** there is no foreign key from `owner_id` to `auth.users`. Prisma rejects cross-schema references (error P4002). Deleting an auth user therefore does not cascade to their rows.

## 4. Seed and reset results

- **Seed:** `prisma db seed` creates 2 auth users with fixed UUIDs and 4 notes with fixed ids and timestamps. It is idempotent. Running it twice gives the same state.
- **Fingerprint:** `scripts/fingerprint.ts` hashes columns, indexes, RLS flags, policies, grants, migration list, note rows, and auth user ids and emails.

| State | Fingerprint |
|---|---|
| Baseline | `73d12d22e5a67732` |
| After adding a stray table and row | `febc49f277be3cc2` (drift detected) |
| After `npm run db:reset` | `73d12d22e5a67732` (identical to baseline; the stray table is gone) |

- **`npm run db:reset`** runs `supabase db reset`, then the shadow DB prep, `prisma migrate deploy` and the seed. It takes about two minutes.
- **`prisma migrate reset` was not run.** Prisma blocks it for AI agents unless you give explicit consent in your own words, and the guard exited without resetting anything. I did not work around it. The first attempt used a flag that does not exist (`--skip-seed`), so ignore any run where the fingerprint did not change.

## 5. RLS tests and security findings

`npm run rls:check` ran **35 of 35 checks passing.** As a negative control, I disabled RLS and the same script failed 18 of 35, so the tests do catch leaks. I re-enabled RLS and reseeded before the final clean run.

**What passed**
- **Unauthenticated:** anon API reads and writes fail with `42501 permission denied`. Prisma as the `anon` role is also denied.
- **User isolation (A and B, symmetric):**
  - Each user sees only their own 2 rows.
  - Reading another user's row by id returns 0 rows.
  - Updating or deleting another user's row affects 0 rows, and the data is unchanged.
  - Inserting a row owned by the other user is rejected by the policy.
  - Reassigning an own row to the other user is also rejected.
  - Inserting and deleting an own row is allowed.
- **Prisma with RLS:** inside a transaction that runs `SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` with the JWT claims set, Prisma returns only the caller's rows. It cannot update, delete or forge another user's rows. Afterwards the role and user do not leak out of the transaction.
- **Storage:**
  - A private bucket can be created and written by the service role.
  - An authenticated user with no storage policy is denied.
  - An anonymous download is denied.
  - A signed URL created on the server works without credentials (HTTP 200).

**Findings**
1. **The default Prisma connection bypasses RLS.** It connects as `postgres`, which is not a superuser but has `BYPASSRLS`. It saw all 4 rows. `service_role` bypasses RLS too. RLS only protects the `anon` and `authenticated` roles, which is why `withRls` switches role per transaction.
2. **RLS trusts whatever identity you give it.** Passing an unverified, client-supplied user id to `withRls` returned the other user's rows. The id must come from a token verified server-side. The script verifies the token with Supabase Auth, and a tampered token is rejected.
3. **Secrets:** a scan of the source files outside `.env` found neither the service-role key nor the database password. The service-role key and `DATABASE_URL` must stay server-only; only the anon key is browser-safe.
4. `npm audit` for the sandbox reports 0 vulnerabilities.

## 6. Exact reproduction commands

From a clean machine with Docker Desktop running:

```bash
cd ~/ezyfusion-infra-sandbox && npm install && cp .env.example .env
```
```bash
npx supabase start
```
```bash
npx supabase status -o json
```

Copy `ANON_KEY` and `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from that output into `.env`. Then:

```bash
npm run db:reset && npm run rls:check
```

Other scripts: `npm run db:check` (Prisma connectivity), `npm run db:fingerprint`, `npm run supabase:stop`.

If the stack is already up (as it is now), `npm run db:reset && npm run rls:check` is enough. After a failed `rls:check`, run `npm run db:reset` or the seed again before rerunning.

## 7. Remaining blockers

None block a start, but note:

- **First `supabase start` downloads about 8 GB of images and took about 10 minutes.** They are cached now. Do this before the assessment.
- **Docker is allotted 8 GB.** That is enough for the nine services plus your two Postgres containers, but not generous.
- **Never use `prisma migrate reset` here.** Besides the agent guard, it drops the `public` schema and its Supabase grants. Use `npm run db:reset`.

## 8. Not verified

- **No Next.js integration.** I did not test `@supabase/ssr` cookies, middleware or `proxy.ts`.
- **No Studio UI session.** Studio was checked by HTTP only.
- **Email flows are untested.** Confirmations are off locally. Mailpit is up but unused.
- **Realtime and storage policies.** Realtime is untested, and I wrote no custom storage policies, only the default deny.

I left the stack running. Stop it with `npm run supabase:stop` in `~/ezyfusion-infra-sandbox` when you are done.

---
title: cookies
description: API Reference for the cookies function.
---

`cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

export default async function Page() {
  const cookieStore = await cookies()
  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
  return '...'
}
```

```js filename="app/page.js" switcher
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

export default async function Page() {
  const cookieStore = await cookies()
  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
  return '...'
}
```

## Reference

### Methods

The following methods are available:

| Method                      | Return Type      | Description                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get('name')`               | Object           | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value.            |
| `getAll()`                  | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name.                         |
| `has('name')`               | Boolean          | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists.      |
| `set(name, value, options)` | -                | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. |
| `delete(name)`              | -                | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie.                                   |
| `toString()`                | String           | Returns a string representation of the cookies.                                 |

### Options

When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported:

| Option        | Type                                   | Description                                                                        |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | String                                 | Specifies the name of the cookie.                                                  |
| `value`       | String                                 | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie.                                    |
| `expires`     | Date                                   | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire.                                |
| `maxAge`      | Number                                 | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds.                                             |
| `domain`      | String                                 | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available.                                |
| `path`        | String, default: `'/'`                 | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain.                    |
| `secure`      | Boolean                                | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security.         |
| `httpOnly`    | Boolean                                | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access.              |
| `sameSite`    | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior.                                 |
| `priority`    | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority                                                    |
| `partitioned` | Boolean                                | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). |

content.text:
# Cycle 3 report: full-stack integration

**GO.** All checks below were executed. The caveats are in section 7.

## 1. Files created

All files are in `~/ezyfusion-integration-sandbox/app` (Next 16.4.2, React 19.3.0, `@supabase/ssr` 0.12.7, Prisma 7.10.1). The infra and UI sandboxes were only read.

- **Supabase clients:**
  - `src/lib/supabase/browser.ts` (anon key only)
  - `src/lib/supabase/server.ts` (a Server Component client plus a Route Handler client that collects cookie writes)
- **Session refresh and guard:** `src/proxy.ts` (token refresh, plus a redirect from `/notes` when there is no session)
- **Server modules:**
  - `src/server/auth.ts` (`verifyUser` via `getUser()`, and the `AuthedUser` type)
  - `src/server/db.ts` (Prisma plus the RLS transaction wrapper `withUser`)
  - `src/server/notes.ts` (data functions, each taking an `AuthedUser`)
  - `src/server/http.ts` (same-origin check, UUID check)
- **Routes:** `auth/login` and `auth/logout` (POST); `api/notes` (GET, POST) and `api/notes/[id]` (GET, DELETE)
- **Pages:** `/`, `/login`, `/notes`, and a client `session-probe.tsx` that reads the session through the browser client
- **Config:** `prisma/schema.prisma` (a mirror of the infra schema), `prisma.config.ts`, `.env.example`
- **Scripts:** `scripts/integration-test.mts`, `scripts/write-env.mts`

## 2. Authentication and session flow

- **Login:** a plain HTML form POSTs to `/auth/login`. The server calls `signInWithPassword`, and the session cookies (`sb-127-auth-token`) are set on a 303 redirect. Only a generic error is shown on failure.
- **Cookies:** `Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, and the response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` (the library requires this). Tokens never pass through page JavaScript on the way in.
- **Per request:** the proxy refreshes the session. Server Components and handlers then call `getUser()`, which asks the Auth server to validate the token. This catches revoked sessions, which `getSession()` would not.
- **Logout:** `signOut({ scope: "local" })` revokes that session on the server and clears the cookies.
- **Browser client:** reads the same cookie session. In a real browser, after login it showed `user-a@sandbox.test`.
- **State-changing routes** require a same-origin `Origin` header. API writes also require `application/json`.

## 3. Prisma integration approach

- The Prisma schema is a copy of the infra sandbox's. Migrations stay in the infra sandbox, and this app only runs `prisma generate`.
- The connection role (`postgres`) bypasses RLS, so the Prisma client is not exported. Every query goes through `withUser(user, fn)`. That wrapper runs `SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` and sets the JWT claims inside a transaction.
- `listNotes` has no owner filter in its code. Isolation comes from the database RLS policies.
- The server-only database modules (`import "server-only"`) are also guarded. I added a temporary client file importing the DB code, and the production build failed with the "server-only" error. I removed the file afterwards.
- The service-role key is not in this app's environment at all.

## 4. Authorization enforcement

- **No client-supplied identity is trusted.** `AuthedUser` can only be produced from `getUser()`, and data functions require it, so an id taken from a query, body or header cannot be passed in by mistake.
- **Mismatched owner:** a supplied `ownerId` that differs from the session returns 403. Another user's note id returns 404, the same as a missing note, so there is no existence leak.
- **Creates:** the owner is always the session user.
- **Layers:** the proxy redirect is a convenience. The real checks are in every handler and in the database.

## 5. Security test results

`npm run test:integration` makes real HTTP requests against the production build and the live Supabase stack, with no mocks. **39 of 39 passed.** The same 39 passed from a clean-room copy.

- **Unauthenticated:** `/notes` redirects to `/login`, and the API returns 401.
- **Login and CSRF:** a wrong password gives a generic 303 with no cookie. A foreign or missing `Origin` gives 403.
- **User isolation:**
  - A sees only A's 2 notes, and B sees only B's.
  - A reading or deleting B's note gets 404, and B's note survives.
  - Manipulated parameters did not expose anything:
    - `?ownerId=<B>` returns 403.
    - Spoofed identity headers are ignored.
    - An SQL-injection-shaped id returns 400 or 403.
    - A POST with `ownerId=<B>` returns 403.
- **Own writes:** create and delete work, and the owner comes from the session.
- **Token tampering:**
  - An access token edited to claim B is rejected.
  - An edited `user` object in the cookie is ignored (A's rows still returned).
  - A token for B signed with the wrong secret is rejected.
  - An expired token with a bad refresh token gives API 401 and a page redirect.
  - A garbage cookie gives 401, not 500.
- **Session invalidation:**
  - After logout, replaying the old cookie returns 401.
  - A global sign-out from another device made two still-unexpired sessions return 401.
- **Secrets in client bundles:** I scanned 43 client files, the prerendered output and the served HTML. I found 0 occurrences of the service-role key, the DB URL or password, the JWT secret, `DATABASE_URL` or `SERVICE_ROLE`. A positive control found the public anon key, so the scanner works.
- **Real browser:** login by form, notes rendered, the browser client showed the email, logout redirected to `/login`, and the API then returned 401.

**One test I corrected.** `/notes?ownerId=<B>` first failed my assertion because the status was 200, not 404. With Partial Prerendering the status is already sent when the page decides it's not found, so it cannot change. The body contained no notes and no email, so I changed the test to assert on data, not status.

**Other validation:** lint, typecheck and production build pass. The infra DB fingerprint is unchanged (`73d12d22e5a67732`) after all tests. Unrelated Docker resources are unchanged.

## 6. Reproduction commands

With Docker Desktop running and the infra stack up (`cd ~/ezyfusion-infra-sandbox && npm run db:reset` if the DB state is unknown):

```bash
cd ~/ezyfusion-integration-sandbox/app && npm ci && npm run env:local && npm run prisma:generate
```
```bash
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run build
```
```bash
npm run start:test
```

Then, in a second terminal:

```bash
cd ~/ezyfusion-integration-sandbox/app && npm run test:integration
```

The app runs on port 3200 (port 3000 is yours). Demo login: `user-a@sandbox.test` or `user-b@sandbox.test` (password `sandbox-password-a` or `-b`, local seed values).

## 7. Caveats

- **The connection role bypasses RLS.** Protection depends on every query going through `withUser`. A least-privilege login role without `BYPASSRLS` would be safer, but it needs an infra change that I did not make.
- **Cookies are not `HttpOnly`.** That is the library default, so the browser client can read them. They are also not `Secure` on local HTTP and must be in production.
- **Not covered:** login rate limiting or lockout, email confirmation (off locally), password reset, Realtime and custom Storage policies.
- **Hydration timing.** In the Browser pane, which may throttle a background page, the streamed client component did not hydrate until I clicked it.
- **Prisma schema drift.** The Prisma schema is a mirror, so it can drift from the infra schema. Keep one source of truth in the real project.
- **Dependency audit.** There are 0 production findings and 5 high dev-only findings (the same `braces` chain as before, via the lint config).

# EzyFusion — Execute Billing Now

The assessment is active. The exact Section 3 contract is provided below. Do not search for the brief or ask for it again.

Create the assessment workspace separately from all preparation sandboxes.

Implement `src/lib/billing.ts` as a pure module, with no Next.js, React, Prisma, Supabase or I/O dependencies.

## Exact TypeScript Contract

```ts
export type InvoiceKind = 'deposit' | 'rent'

export interface ScheduledInvoice {
  kind: InvoiceKind
  periodIndex: number | null
  periodStart: string | null
  periodEnd: string | null
  dueDate: string
  amountSen: number
}

export function generateSchedule(lease: {
  startDate: string
  endDate: string
  monthlyRentSen: number
  depositSen: number
}): ScheduledInvoice[]

export type InvoiceStatus =
  | 'paid'
  | 'partially_paid'
  | 'unpaid'
  | 'overdue'

export function invoiceStatus(
  invoice: {
    dueDate: string
    amountSen: number
    paidSen: number
  },
  now: Date,
): InvoiceStatus

export function parseRinggitToSen(input: string): number
```

## generateSchedule Rules

- Throw an Error for invalid YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates, end before start, monthlyRentSen not a positive integer, or depositSen not a non-negative integer.
- If depositSen > 0, emit a deposit invoice first, due on startDate, with null period fields.
- Rent anchors are calculated from the ORIGINAL start date plus k calendar months, clamped to the final day of shorter months.
- Never calculate an anchor from the previous anchor.
- Rent period k starts at anchor k and ends on the day before anchor k+1, inclusive.
- Generate a rent period for each anchor on or before endDate.
- The final period ends at endDate.
- If the final period is shorter than the full period, prorate monthlyRentSen × days used / full period days, rounded half up to the nearest sen.
- Other periods charge full monthly rent.
- Order: deposit first, then rent by periodIndex.

### Required worked example

Input:
```json
{
  "startDate": "2026-01-31",
  "endDate": "2026-07-15",
  "monthlyRentSen": 150000,
  "depositSen": 300000
}
```

Expected invoices:

| Kind | Index | Start | End | Due | AmountSen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| deposit | null | null | null | 2026-01-31 | 300000 |
| rent | 0 | 2026-01-31 | 2026-02-27 | 2026-01-31 | 150000 |
| rent | 1 | 2026-02-28 | 2026-03-30 | 2026-02-28 | 150000 |
| rent | 2 | 2026-03-31 | 2026-04-29 | 2026-03-31 | 150000 |
| rent | 3 | 2026-04-30 | 2026-05-30 | 2026-04-30 | 150000 |
| rent | 4 | 2026-05-31 | 2026-06-29 | 2026-05-31 | 150000 |
| rent | 5 | 2026-06-30 | 2026-07-15 | 2026-06-30 | 77419 |

The final period uses 16 of 31 days.

## invoiceStatus Rules

Apply in this exact order:

1. `paid` if paidSen >= amountSen.
2. `overdue` if today's Malaysia calendar date is after dueDate.
3. `partially_paid` if paidSen > 0.
4. Otherwise `unpaid`.

Malaysia timezone: `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur` (UTC+8).

An invoice due 2026-03-01 becomes overdue at 2026-03-02 00:00 Malaysia time, which is 2026-03-01T16:00:00Z.

Do not use the process or viewer timezone.

## parseRinggitToSen Rules

Accept digits with optional comma thousands separators, each group exactly three digits, and an optional decimal part of one or two digits.

Ignore whitespace surrounding the value.

Valid:
- "1,500.50" → 150050
- "1.15" → 115
- "7" → 700

Invalid, must throw Error:
- ""
- "-5"
- "1.234"
- "1e3"
- "RM 10"
- "1,23"

Reject unsafe integer overflow rather than silently losing precision.

## Tests

Write comprehensive tests for:
- Exact worked example
- Jan 29/30/31 anchors
- Leap years
- One-day leases
- Inclusive period boundaries
- Proration and half-up rounding
- Invalid dates and amounts
- Invoice status precedence
- Malaysia midnight boundary
- Valid and invalid money strings

Run tests under:
- TZ=UTC
- TZ=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur
- TZ=America/New_York

Report files created and exact test results.

Do not start database, payments, UI or other assessment features yet. Do not commit or deploy.

The full assessment also requires Supabase SQL migrations as the database source of truth, Prisma server access, integer-sen money storage, date columns for calendar dates, and timestamptz for instants. We will provide the remaining contracts in the next cycle.

Preserve this AI session for export into ai-logs/.
</pasted_content id="a84f">
