# REVIEW.md — Code review of the teammate's snippets (Assessment Part B)

Scope: the three snippets in the assessment document. Assumptions, as given: Prisma connects as the database owner (so it **bypasses RLS**), `createClient()` returns the request's Supabase server client, `allocate(tx, paymentId)` is correct.

**Line numbers.** All numbers below are the line numbers of the original assessment document: late fees 306–357, webhook 360–399, collections 402–416. They were derived from those three ranges. The ranges are contiguous slices of the supplied snippets: the late-fees and webhook ranges start at the first `import` and end at the final `}`; the collections range starts at its `// app/(staff)/…` comment. The path comment on the first two snippets is therefore not numbered. The original text itself was not available while writing this, so these numbers could not be checked against it directly. Every finding also quotes the code so it can be located without the numbers.

Severity scale: **Critical** = exploitable data/money loss or privilege escalation; **High** = wrong money, duplicate effects, secret disclosure or a broken endpoint; **Medium** = contract violations with a real but narrower impact; **Low** = robustness / status-code issues.

## Summary

| # | Sev | File | Lines | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | late-fees | 316–319 | Manager role read from client-writable `user_metadata` |
| 2 | Critical | late-fees | 322–326 | No organization scoping: fees on any organization's lease |
| 3 | Critical | collections | 403, 407, 411 | Public server action; client-supplied `orgId`, no authentication |
| 4 | Critical | webhook | 379–398 | Bill status checked outside the transaction, no lock: concurrent callbacks double-credit |
| 5 | High | webhook | 374 | Logs the full payload and the *valid* signature |
| 6 | High | webhook | 391 | Payment amount taken from the callback, never compared with the bill |
| 7 | High | late-fees | 332–350 | Not idempotent, no lock: every call charges the same invoice again |
| 8 | High | late-fees | 337–350, 354–357 | Lazy Prisma promises + `nextReference`: identical references; no transaction |
| 9 | High | collections | 409, 412 | Months and bounds use the database timezone, not Malaysia time |
| 10 | High | late-fees | 342, 345, 355–356 | `late_fee`, `reference`, `createdAt` do not exist in the required invoice model |
| 11 | Medium | webhook | 377 | `paid=false` ignored: bill never becomes `failed`; unknown bill not 404 |
| 12 | Medium | webhook | 373 | Signature compared with `!==` instead of `timingSafeEqual` |
| 13 | Medium | webhook | 392 | `receivedAt` is the server clock, not the gateway's `paid_at` |
| 14 | Medium | collections | 409, 413 | Months without payments are missing |
| 15 | Medium | late-fees | 335–336 | Floating-point money and a 0.5 % free pass |
| 16 | Medium | webhook | 386–394 | `unapplied_sen` (NOT NULL) is not set on the payment |
| 17 | Low | late-fees | 316–319 | Unauthenticated request answered 403 instead of 401 |
| 18 | Low | all | 321–323, 366, 407–412 | Unvalidated input becomes a 500 |
| 19 | Low | collections | 408, 415 | `SUM(bigint)` is `numeric`; `Number()` with no overflow check |

---

## 1. Critical — manager role comes from `user_metadata` (late-fees, L316–319)

```ts
const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()                 // L316-317
if (user?.user_metadata.role !== 'manager') {                            // L318
  return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Forbidden' }, { status: 403 })      // L319
}
```
**Failure.** `user_metadata` is writable by the user themselves. Any signed-in tenant runs `supabase.auth.updateUser({ data: { role: 'manager' } })` in the browser and passes this check. The assessment rule is that roles come from `memberships` (and tenants from `tenants.user_id`), never from user metadata.
**Fix.** Use only the verified `user.id`, then load the role from the database: `prisma.membership.findUnique({ where: { userId_orgId: { userId: user.id, orgId: lease.orgId } } })` and require `role === 'manager'`.

## 2. Critical — no organization scoping on the lease (late-fees, L322–326)

```ts
const lease = await prisma.lease.findUnique({ where: { id: leaseId }, include: {...} })   // L322-326
```
**Failure.** Prisma runs as the owner, so RLS does not help. Any caller who passes check #1 (including a manager of organization A) can POST to a lease id of organization B and create fees on it. The 404 vs 200 difference also confirms which lease ids exist.
**Fix.** Scope the lookup by the caller's organizations: `findFirst({ where: { id: leaseId, orgId: { in: managerOrgIds } } })`, where `managerOrgIds` comes from the caller's `manager` memberships; return 404 otherwise. Never trust ids from the request for authorization.

## 3. Critical — public server action with a client-supplied `orgId` (collections, L403, L407, L411)

```ts
'use server'                                                              // L403
export async function getCollections(orgId: string, from: string, to: string) {   // L407
  ... WHERE org_id = ${orgId}::uuid AND status = 'approved'               // L411
```
**Failure.** A `'use server'` export is a public POST endpoint. Nothing here authenticates the caller or checks membership, and Prisma bypasses RLS. Anyone (even without a session) can call it with another organization's UUID and read that organization's monthly revenue.
**Fix.** Authenticate with `supabase.auth.getUser()`, resolve the caller's staff/manager organizations from `memberships`, ignore (or verify) the client `orgId`, and return 401/403 otherwise.

## 4. Critical — webhook checks the bill status outside the transaction, with no lock (webhook, L379–398)

```ts
const bill = await prisma.gatewayBill.findUnique(...)                     // L379
if (bill.status === 'paid') return NextResponse.json({ ok: true })        // L381
await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { ...                             // L383
  await tx.gatewayBill.update(... status: 'paid')                         // L384
  const payment = await tx.payment.create(...)                            // L385
  await allocate(tx, payment.id)                                          // L396
```
**Failure.** Two `paid=true` callbacks 5 ms apart (the gateway retries) both read `pending` at L379–381 before either commits. Both enter the transaction: the bill is "paid" twice and **two approved online payments** are created and allocated, so the tenant is credited twice. If `UNIQUE(payments.gateway_bill_id)` exists, the second transaction instead fails with an unhandled unique violation → HTTP 500 → the gateway retries again. The webhook also races with manual payments: no per-lease lock is taken before `allocate`.
**Fix.** In one transaction: take the same per-lease row lock manual payments use (`SELECT … FROM leases WHERE id = … FOR UPDATE`) first, re-read the bill **inside** the lock, return 200 if it is already `paid`, create exactly one payment, and keep `UNIQUE(gateway_bill_id)` as the last line of defence (handle its violation as "already paid").

## 5. High — logs the full callback and the valid signature (webhook, L374)

```ts
console.error('Invalid signature', { fields, expected })                  // L374
```
**Failure.** `expected` is the correct HMAC **for the attacker-supplied fields**. Anyone who can read the logs (log aggregator, support staff, a leaked log bucket) can submit a callback with the fields they want, read `expected` from the log, and resend it with that signature: a forged "paid" callback. The log line also stores payment/customer data from `fields`.
**Fix.** Never log the secret, the expected signature or the payload. Log only a constant reason and a request id.

## 6. High — payment amount comes from the callback (webhook, L391)

```ts
amountSen: BigInt(fields.paid_amount),                                    // L391
```
**Failure.** The amount is never compared with `bill.amount_sen`. A callback for a RM 10 bill with `paid_amount=99999999` (validly signed by a gateway fault or a leaked key) credits RM 999,999.99; a short payment settles the whole bill. `BigInt('abc')`, `BigInt('10.5')` or an empty value throws `SyntaxError` → 500 and endless gateway retries; zero or negative values reach the database.
**Fix.** Require `paid_amount` to equal the canonical string of `bill.amountSen` (otherwise 422, no changes) and create the payment from `bill.amountSen`.

## 7. High — fee creation is not idempotent and not serialized (late-fees, L332–350)

```ts
for (const invoice of lease.invoices) { ... fees.push(prisma.invoice.create(...)) }   // L332-L350
```
**Failure.** Nothing records that an invoice already received a late fee. Every POST (double-click, client retry, a scheduled job) creates another fee for every still-unpaid invoice, so the same arrears are charged repeatedly. Two concurrent POSTs both read the same state and both create fees; no per-lease lock is used.
**Fix.** Link each fee to its source invoice with a unique constraint (one fee per source invoice), or skip invoices that already have one, and do the read-and-create in one transaction under the per-lease lock.

## 8. High — lazy Prisma promises make `nextReference` return the same value (late-fees, L337–350, L354–357)

```ts
fees.push(prisma.invoice.create({ data: { ..., reference: await nextReference(lease.orgId) } }))   // L337-L349
await Promise.all(fees)                                                                              // L350
async function nextReference(orgId) { const last = await prisma.invoice.findFirst(...); return `INV-${...+ 1}` }   // L354-L357
```
**Failure.** Prisma queries are lazy: `prisma.invoice.create(...)` does not execute until it is awaited or `.then` is called, which happens only in `Promise.all` at L350. Every `await nextReference()` in the loop therefore sees the same "last" invoice, so all fees in one request get the **same reference** (a duplicate, or a unique-constraint failure that leaves some fees created). Two concurrent requests collide the same way. `Promise.all` is not a transaction, so one failure leaves a partial set. `parseInt(last.reference.slice(4))` yields `NaN` for any non-`INV-` reference.
**Fix.** Generate references atomically (a per-organization counter row updated with `UPDATE … RETURNING`, or a sequence) and create all fees inside a single `prisma.$transaction`.

```sql
to_char(date_trunc('month', received_at), 'YYYY-MM')                                   -- L409
AND received_at >= ${from}::date AND received_at < ${to}::date + interval '1 month'    -- L412
```

# DECISIONS.md

Each answer is at most 150 words. Paths and line numbers refer to the repository as submitted (verified mechanically against the files; see the end of this document).

## 1. Two `paid=true` callbacks arrive 5 ms apart

Both pass signature verification (`src/app/api/webhooks/gateway/route.ts:33`) and call `applyGatewayCallback` (`src/server/domain/gateway.ts:56`). The pre-lookup at `:66` only fetches the bill's lease id and decides nothing. Each opens a transaction (`:70`) whose first statement is `lockLease` (`:71`), a `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the lease row (`src/server/domain/payments.ts:16-17`). Callback A holds the lock; B waits. A re-reads the bill under the lock (`gateway.ts:72`), sees it unpaid, creates the single payment (`:89-91`) and marks the bill paid (`:96`). B resumes after A commits, re-reads (`:72`), sees `paid`, and returns at `:85` without writing. Backstop: `UNIQUE (gateway_bill_id)` (`supabase/migrations/20261020000100_schema.sql:118`), handled at `gateway.ts:102-105`. Proven by `tests/api/gateway.test.ts:370`.

## 2. Two staff record RM 800 and RM 700 concurrently, RM 1,000 remaining

Both requests resolve access (`src/server/domain/payments.ts:73`) and enter a transaction (`:86`). Its first statement, `lockLease` (`:87`, SQL at `:16-17`), is `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the lease row, so the second request waits. The winner (say RM 800) computes the maximum payable, remaining minus pending (`:88-89`, `src/lib/allocation.ts:55`), which is RM 1,000; it passes the check at `:90`, inserts a `pending_verification` payment (`:92`) and commits. The loser then gets the lock, and `leaseState` now counts that payment in `pendingTotalSen` (query at `:32`), so its maximum is RM 200 and RM 700 fails with HTTP 422 at `:90`. The preventing lock is the PostgreSQL row lock on `public.leases`, shared by record, approve, reject, void and the webhook (`:12-15`). Proven by `tests/api/concurrency-reports-slips.test.ts:19`.

## 3. Where code calculates "today" or converts between a calendar date and an instant

The business timezone is Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (UTC+8, no DST): due dates, overdue status and reports are Malaysian calendar concepts.

- Today / status: `src/lib/billing.ts:23,151-165`; `src/lib/malaysia.ts:9`, used at `src/server/domain/gateway.ts:19,25` and `src/server/domain/views.ts:76,112`.
- Gateway `paid_at` (+0800) → UTC: `malaysia.ts:18-27`, used at `gateway.ts:62`.
- Reports: `src/server/domain/reports.ts:16,28-33` (SQL `at time zone`).
- UI display/input: `src/lib/format-my.ts:25-44,59-60`; `src/components/lease/payment-form.tsx:41,63,102`.
- API instants need an explicit offset: `src/server/domain/convert.ts:20-23`.

Calendar dates have no timezone, so they map to UTC midnight: `convert.ts:16,18`, `scripts/seed.mts:108`, `src/lib/format.ts:59-60`; the picker uses local date parts (`src/lib/date.ts:13-22`). Instants are `timestamptz` (`schema.sql:109`).

## 4. Everything that bypasses RLS, and what enforces authorization

The AI-log references in `DECISIONS.md` are placeholders. Lint, typecheck and build pass, and no application code was changed.

## `REVIEW.md`

It contains 19 findings, ordered Critical, High, Medium, then Low. Each has the line numbers, a concrete failure scenario and a specific fix.

- **Critical:**
  - The manager role is read from client-writable `user_metadata`.
  - The lease lookup has no organization scoping.
  - The collections server action is public and trusts a client-supplied `orgId`.
  - The webhook checks the bill status outside the transaction with no lock, so concurrent callbacks double-credit.
- **High:**
  - The webhook logs the payload and the valid expected signature.
  - The payment amount comes from the callback.
  - Late fees are not idempotent.
  - `nextReference` combined with lazy Prisma promises gives identical references and no transaction.
  - Collections use the database timezone, not Malaysia.
  - `late_fee`, `reference` and `createdAt` do not exist in the invoice model.
- **Medium:**
  - `paid=false` is ignored.
  - The signature is compared with `!==`.
  - `receivedAt` uses the server clock instead of `paid_at`.
  - Zero-payment months are missing.
  - Late-fee money uses floating point with a 0.5% free pass.
  - `unapplied_sen` is not set on the payment.
- **Low:** 403 instead of 401 for unauthenticated requests, unvalidated input becoming a 500, and an unchecked `Number()` conversion of `SUM(bigint)`.

**Line numbers.** I derived them from your three ranges. Each range matches a contiguous slice of the snippet you pasted:
- Late fees, 306–357: starts at the first `import` and ends at the closing `}`.
- Webhook, 360–399: same.
- Collections, 402–416: starts at the file-path comment.

The pasted late-fees and webhook snippets each have one more line than those ranges, so I assumed their file-path comment line is not numbered. This is stated at the top of `REVIEW.md`, and every finding also quotes the code. If you send the original numbered text, I can check them in minutes.

## `DECISIONS.md`

Six answers of 97, 116, 84, 78, 88 and 138 words, all under the 150-word limit. Every `path:line` citation points to a real line and I confirmed the cited line content for the key ones.

- `DECISIONS.md` question 6 has two real mistakes from this session. Both are cited to repository lines, and the log references are bracketed placeholders for you to fill:
  - The first schema guessed payment enumerations, corrected by the forward migration.
  - The first seed created approved payments without allocations, corrected by the domain-based seed.
- No `ai-logs/` folder exists yet, so I could not confirm them against exported logs. Export the session and fill in both placeholders before submission.

# EzyFusion — property management and rent collection

A multi-organization rent-collection app: leases and invoice schedules, manual and online payments with allocation, manager approval workflow, a tenant portal, and a payment-gateway webhook. Built for the EzyFusion technical assessment.

## Stack

- Next.js 16 (App Router, Cache Components), TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui on Base UI
- Supabase (local, Docker): PostgreSQL 17, Auth, Storage, Data API with Row Level Security
- Prisma 7 for server-side data access (connects as the database owner; see Security notes)
- Vitest for unit/DB/API tests, `playwright-core` + Chrome for browser tests

**The SQL migrations in `supabase/migrations/` are the only source of schema changes.** Prisma Migrate is never used; `prisma/schema.prisma` mirrors the database and `npm run db:check` verifies they agree.

## Setup (exact commands)

Prerequisites: Node.js 24, Docker Desktop running (at least ~8 GB memory allocated), free ports 54321-54324 and 3000.

```bash
npx supabase start
npx supabase db reset
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
npm run seed
npm run build && npm start
```

Then open http://localhost:3000.

Notes:
- `.env.example` already contains working **local-only** values (the Supabase CLI's well-known development defaults). No edits are needed for a local run. Get the live values any time with `npx supabase status -o env`.
- The first `supabase start` downloads about 8 GB of Docker images.
- If `npx supabase` runs before `npm install`, npx downloads the CLI on the fly (latest version). `npm install` first uses the version pinned in `package-lock.json`; both work with the migrations here.
- `npm install` runs `prisma generate` (postinstall); no database is needed for that.
- `npm run seed` is idempotent. For a pristine state run `npx supabase db reset` first.

## Environment variables (`.env.example`)

| Variable | Purpose | Browser-safe? |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase API URL | yes |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Publishable key for browser/SSR clients (RLS protects every table) | yes |
| `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | Bypasses RLS: seed, orphan-slip cleanup | **no, server only** |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Prisma runtime connection (database owner) | **no, server only** |
| `DIRECT_URL` | Direct connection for Prisma CLI commands | **no, server only** |
| `GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY` | HMAC key for gateway webhook signatures | **no, server only** |
| `SEED_PASSWORD` | Password for every seeded account (seed script only) | no (never sent to the browser) |
| `WEBHOOK_URL` (optional) | Target of `gateway-sim.mjs` (default `http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway`) | n/a |

## Seed accounts

All accounts use the password **`Passw0rd!local`** (set by `SEED_PASSWORD` in `.env.example`; local test data only).

| Organization | Email | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Northwind Properties | manager@northwind.test | manager |
| Northwind Properties | staff@northwind.test | staff |
| Northwind Properties | aisyah@northwind.test | tenant (Aisyah Rahman, unit A-12-3) |
| Northwind Properties | ben@northwind.test | tenant (Ben Lim, unit B-05-1) |
| Northwind Properties | probe@northwind.test | tenant (Probe Tenant, unit C-01-7) |
| Beta Realty | manager@beta.test | manager |
| Beta Realty | chen@beta.test | tenant (Chen Wei, unit KL-1) |

Seeded data: 2 organizations, 5 units (Northwind D-03-2 has no lease), 4 leases, 37 invoices (generated by `generateSchedule()`), and Aisyah's two approved payments (RM 3,000.00 cash recorded by the manager; RM 2,000.00 bank transfer recorded by staff with a slip and approved by the manager), allocated to her invoices. The Northwind collections report for Jan-Mar 2026 is 300000 / 0 / 200000 sen.

## Features

- **Billing rules** (`src/lib/billing.ts`): `generateSchedule`, `invoiceStatus`, `parseRinggitToSen` (integer sen, Malaysia time, month-end clamping, half-up proration).
- **Authentication:** email/password login, SSR session cookies, logout, role-aware navigation. Roles come from `memberships` and `tenants.user_id`, never from `user_metadata`. The API also accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Staff / manager:** dashboard (overdue invoices, six-month collections), leases list and detail (invoices, payments, slip links), manual payment form (cash / bank transfer with slip upload), manager approve / reject / void.
- **Tenant:** own leases, invoices, payments, amount due now, "Pay now" (creates a gateway bill), return page, and phone-number update directly through the Data API (RLS + column grant).
- **Payments:** allocation by due date (deposit before rent, then period), payment cap (remaining balance minus pending), per-lease row lock for all money-changing operations, voiding.
- **Online payments:** `POST /api/leases/:id/gateway-bills`, signed webhook `POST /api/webhooks/gateway` (idempotent, concurrency-safe), `/payments/return` (read-only, never settles), simulator `node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false]`.
- **Database:** RLS on every public table, tenant/staff/manager policies, append-only `audit_log`, private `payment-slips` bucket with organization-scoped Storage policies.

API: `POST /api/leases`, `GET /api/leases/:id`, `POST /api/leases/:id/payments`, `POST /api/leases/:id/gateway-bills`, `POST /api/payments/:id/approve|reject|void`, `GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM`, `POST /api/webhooks/gateway`.

## Tests

The app and the Supabase stack must be running for the integration suites (`npm run build && npm start -- -p 3300`, `npx supabase start`, `npx supabase db reset`, `npm run seed`).

| Command | What it runs |
|---|---|
| `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` | static checks and production build |
| `npm test` | unit tests (billing, allocation, signature, formatting) |
| `npm run test:tz` | the unit tests under `TZ=UTC`, `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur`, `America/New_York` |
| `npm run test:db` | schema, RLS, Storage and audit-log tests against the local database |
| `npm run test:api` | real HTTP tests incl. concurrency and the webhook (`API_BASE_URL`, default `http://localhost:3300`) |
| `npm run test:ui` | Chrome browser tests (`CHROME_PATH` to override `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/...`) |
| `npm run db:check` | Prisma schema vs. database consistency |

Integration tests create and clean up their own leases/payments, but audit-log rows cannot be deleted: run `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed` for a pristine database.

## Security notes

- Prisma connects as the database owner and **bypasses RLS**: every server query is authorized in code (`src/server/domain/access.ts`, `viewer.ts`).
- Browser bundles contain only the Supabase URL and publishable key (checked by `test:ui` and by scanning `.next/static`).
- `audit_log` is append-only via triggers; a superuser/table owner can still change the trigger through DDL.
- The per-lease lock is a convention: any new code that changes payments, allocations or bills must call `lockLease()` first.

## Known limitations

- No UI to create leases, tenants or units (the lease API exists); no registration, password reset, or staff management.
- No rate limiting on login or the webhook; cookie-authenticated API calls do not refresh expired access tokens (page requests do, via `src/proxy.ts`).
- Money is displayed in MYR only; the dashboard is tables with simple bars (no charts or filters).
- Unapplied online funds are never auto-applied later (voiding another payment does not reallocate them).
- Some tests depend on the current Malaysia date (they build leases around "today") and the browser tests need Google Chrome installed.
- Local development stack only: nothing is configured for deployment; Supabase analytics and the edge runtime are disabled in `supabase/config.toml` to save memory.
- `ai-logs/` contains no transcripts yet; they must be exported manually (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## What would be implemented next

Lease/tenant/unit management screens, account self-service (password reset), rate limiting and webhook replay protection, a database-level balance guard (trigger) as a second layer under the lease lock, charts and filters on the dashboard, automatic application of unapplied online funds under a defined policy, and CI running the full suite.

- `npm run seed` is idempotent. For a pristine state run `npx supabase db reset` first.

## Environment variables (`.env.example`)

| Variable | Purpose | Browser-safe? |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase API URL | yes |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Publishable key for browser/SSR clients (RLS protects every table) | yes |
| `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | Bypasses RLS: seed, orphan-slip cleanup | **no, server only** |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Prisma runtime connection (database owner) | **no, server only** |
| `DIRECT_URL` | Direct connection for Prisma CLI commands | **no, server only** |
| `GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY` | HMAC key for gateway webhook signatures | **no, server only** |
| `SEED_PASSWORD` | Password for every seeded account (seed script only) | no (never sent to the browser) |
| `WEBHOOK_URL` (optional) | Target of `gateway-sim.mjs` (default `http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway`) | n/a |

All accounts use the password **`Passw0rd!local`** (set by `SEED_PASSWORD` in `.env.example`; local test data only).

| Organization | Email | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Northwind Properties | manager@northwind.test | manager |
| Northwind Properties | staff@northwind.test | staff |
| Northwind Properties | aisyah@northwind.test | tenant (Aisyah Rahman, unit A-12-3) |
| Northwind Properties | ben@northwind.test | tenant (Ben Lim, unit B-05-1) |
| Northwind Properties | probe@northwind.test | tenant (Probe Tenant, unit C-01-7) |
| Beta Realty | manager@beta.test | manager |
| Beta Realty | chen@beta.test | tenant (Chen Wei, unit KL-1) |

Seeded data: 2 organizations, 5 units (Northwind D-03-2 has no lease), 4 leases, 37 invoices (generated by `generateSchedule()`), and Aisyah's two approved payments (RM 3,000.00 cash recorded by the manager; RM 2,000.00 bank transfer recorded by staff with a slip and approved by the manager), allocated to her invoices. The Northwind collections report for Jan-Mar 2026 is 300000 / 0 / 200000 sen.

## Features

- **Billing rules** (`src/lib/billing.ts`): `generateSchedule`, `invoiceStatus`, `parseRinggitToSen` (integer sen, Malaysia time, month-end clamping, half-up proration).
- **Authentication:** email/password login, SSR session cookies, logout, role-aware navigation. Roles come from `memberships` and `tenants.user_id`, never from `user_metadata`. The API also accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Staff / manager:** dashboard (overdue invoices, six-month collections), leases list and detail (invoices, payments, slip links), manual payment form (cash / bank transfer with slip upload), manager approve / reject / void.
- **Tenant:** own leases, invoices, payments, amount due now, "Pay now" (creates a gateway bill), return page, and phone-number update directly through the Data API (RLS + column grant).
- **Payments:** allocation by due date (deposit before rent, then period), payment cap (remaining balance minus pending), per-lease row lock for all money-changing operations, voiding.
- **Online payments:** `POST /api/leases/:id/gateway-bills`, signed webhook `POST /api/webhooks/gateway` (idempotent, concurrency-safe), `/payments/return` (read-only, never settles), simulator `node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false]`.
- **Database:** RLS on every public table, tenant/staff/manager policies, append-only `audit_log`, private `payment-slips` bucket with organization-scoped Storage policies.

API: `POST /api/leases`, `GET /api/leases/:id`, `POST /api/leases/:id/payments`, `POST /api/leases/:id/gateway-bills`, `POST /api/payments/:id/approve|reject|void`, `GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM`, `POST /api/webhooks/gateway`.

## Tests

The app and the Supabase stack must be running for the integration suites (`npm run build && npm start -- -p 3300`, `npx supabase start`, `npx supabase db reset`, `npm run seed`).

| Command | What it runs |
|---|---|
| `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` | static checks and production build |
| `npm test` | unit tests (billing, allocation, signature, formatting) |
| `npm run test:tz` | the unit tests under `TZ=UTC`, `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur`, `America/New_York` |
| `npm run test:db` | schema, RLS, Storage and audit-log tests against the local database |
| `npm run test:api` | real HTTP tests incl. concurrency and the webhook (`API_BASE_URL`, default `http://localhost:3300`) |
| `npm run test:ui` | Chrome browser tests (`CHROME_PATH` to override `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/...`) |
| `npm run db:check` | Prisma schema vs. database consistency |

Integration tests create and clean up their own leases/payments, but audit-log rows cannot be deleted: run `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed` for a pristine database.

## Security notes

- Prisma connects as the database owner and **bypasses RLS**: every server query is authorized in code (`src/server/domain/access.ts`, `viewer.ts`).
- Browser bundles contain only the Supabase URL and publishable key (checked by `test:ui` and by scanning `.next/static`).
- `audit_log` is append-only via triggers; a superuser/table owner can still change the trigger through DDL.
- The per-lease lock is a convention: any new code that changes payments, allocations or bills must call `lockLease()` first.

## Known limitations

- No UI to create leases, tenants or units (the lease API exists); no registration, password reset, or staff management.
- No rate limiting on login or the webhook; cookie-authenticated API calls do not refresh expired access tokens (page requests do, via `src/proxy.ts`).
- Money is displayed in MYR only; the dashboard is tables with simple bars (no charts or filters).
- Unapplied online funds are never auto-applied later (voiding another payment does not reallocate them).
- Some tests depend on the current Malaysia date (they build leases around "today") and the browser tests need Google Chrome installed.
- Local development stack only: nothing is configured for deployment; Supabase analytics and the edge runtime are disabled in `supabase/config.toml` to save memory.
- `ai-logs/` contains no transcripts yet; they must be exported manually (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## What would be implemented next

Lease/tenant/unit management screens, account self-service (password reset), rate limiting and webhook replay protection, a database-level balance guard (trigger) as a second layer under the lease lock, charts and filters on the dashboard, automatic application of unapplied online funds under a defined policy, and CI running the full suite.

# EzyFusion — property management and rent collection

A multi-organization rent-collection app: leases and invoice schedules, manual and online payments with allocation, manager approval workflow, a tenant portal, and a payment-gateway webhook. Built for the EzyFusion technical assessment.

## Stack

- Next.js 16 (App Router, Cache Components), TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui on Base UI
- Supabase (local, Docker): PostgreSQL 17, Auth, Storage, Data API with Row Level Security
- Prisma 7 for server-side data access (connects as the database owner; see Security notes)
- Vitest for unit/DB/API tests, `playwright-core` + Chrome for browser tests

**The SQL migrations in `supabase/migrations/` are the only source of schema changes.** Prisma Migrate is never used; `prisma/schema.prisma` mirrors the database and `npm run db:check` verifies they agree.

## Setup (exact commands)

Prerequisites: Node.js 24, Docker Desktop running (at least ~8 GB memory allocated), free ports 54321-54324 and 3000.

```bash
npx supabase start
npx supabase db reset
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
npm run seed
npm run build && npm start
```

Then open http://localhost:3000.

Notes:
- `.env.example` already contains working **local-only** values (the Supabase CLI's well-known development defaults). No edits are needed for a local run. Get the live values any time with `npx supabase status -o env`.
- The first `supabase start` downloads about 8 GB of Docker images.
- If `npx supabase` runs before `npm install`, npx downloads the CLI on the fly (latest version). `npm install` first uses the version pinned in `package-lock.json`; both work with the migrations here.
- `npm install` runs `prisma generate` (postinstall); no database is needed for that.
- `npm run seed` is idempotent. For a pristine state run `npx supabase db reset` first.

## Environment variables (`.env.example`)

| Variable | Purpose | Browser-safe? |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase API URL | yes |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Publishable key for browser/SSR clients (RLS protects every table) | yes |
| `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | Bypasses RLS: seed, orphan-slip cleanup | **no, server only** |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Prisma runtime connection (database owner) | **no, server only** |
| `DIRECT_URL` | Direct connection for Prisma CLI commands | **no, server only** |
| `GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY` | HMAC key for gateway webhook signatures | **no, server only** |
| `SEED_PASSWORD` | Password for every seeded account (seed script only) | no (never sent to the browser) |
| `WEBHOOK_URL` (optional) | Target of `gateway-sim.mjs` (default `http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway`) | n/a |

## Seed accounts

All accounts use the password **`Passw0rd!local`** (set by `SEED_PASSWORD` in `.env.example`; local test data only).

| Organization | Email | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Northwind Properties | manager@northwind.test | manager |
| Northwind Properties | staff@northwind.test | staff |
| Northwind Properties | aisyah@northwind.test | tenant (Aisyah Rahman, unit A-12-3) |
| Northwind Properties | ben@northwind.test | tenant (Ben Lim, unit B-05-1) |
| Northwind Properties | probe@northwind.test | tenant (Probe Tenant, unit C-01-7) |
| Beta Realty | manager@beta.test | manager |
| Beta Realty | chen@beta.test | tenant (Chen Wei, unit KL-1) |

Seeded data: 2 organizations, 5 units (Northwind D-03-2 has no lease), 4 leases, 37 invoices (generated by `generateSchedule()`), and Aisyah's two approved payments (RM 3,000.00 cash recorded by the manager; RM 2,000.00 bank transfer recorded by staff with a slip and approved by the manager), allocated to her invoices. The Northwind collections report for Jan-Mar 2026 is 300000 / 0 / 200000 sen.

## Features

- **Billing rules** (`src/lib/billing.ts`): `generateSchedule`, `invoiceStatus`, `parseRinggitToSen` (integer sen, Malaysia time, month-end clamping, half-up proration).
- **Authentication:** email/password login, SSR session cookies, logout, role-aware navigation. Roles come from `memberships` and `tenants.user_id`, never from `user_metadata`. The API also accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Staff / manager:** dashboard (overdue invoices, six-month collections), leases list and detail (invoices, payments, slip links), manual payment form (cash / bank transfer with slip upload), manager approve / reject / void.
- **Tenant:** own leases, invoices, payments, amount due now, "Pay now" (creates a gateway bill), return page, and phone-number update directly through the Data API (RLS + column grant).
- **Payments:** allocation by due date (deposit before rent, then period), payment cap (remaining balance minus pending), per-lease row lock for all money-changing operations, voiding.
- **Online payments:** `POST /api/leases/:id/gateway-bills`, signed webhook `POST /api/webhooks/gateway` (idempotent, concurrency-safe), `/payments/return` (read-only, never settles), simulator `node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false]`.
- **Database:** RLS on every public table, tenant/staff/manager policies, append-only `audit_log`, private `payment-slips` bucket with organization-scoped Storage policies.

API: `POST /api/leases`, `GET /api/leases/:id`, `POST /api/leases/:id/payments`, `POST /api/leases/:id/gateway-bills`, `POST /api/payments/:id/approve|reject|void`, `GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM`, `POST /api/webhooks/gateway`.

## Tests

The app and the Supabase stack must be running for the integration suites (`npm run build && npm start -- -p 3300`, `npx supabase start`, `npx supabase db reset`, `npm run seed`).

| Command | What it runs |
|---|---|
| `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` | static checks and production build |
| `npm test` | unit tests (billing, allocation, signature, formatting) |
| `npm run test:tz` | the unit tests under `TZ=UTC`, `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur`, `America/New_York` |
| `npm run test:db` | schema, RLS, Storage and audit-log tests against the local database |
| `npm run test:api` | real HTTP tests incl. concurrency and the webhook (`API_BASE_URL`, default `http://localhost:3300`) |
| `npm run test:ui` | Chrome browser tests (`CHROME_PATH` to override `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/...`) |
| `npm run db:check` | Prisma schema vs. database consistency |

Integration tests create and clean up their own leases/payments, but audit-log rows cannot be deleted: run `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed` for a pristine database.

## Security notes

- Prisma connects as the database owner and **bypasses RLS**: every server query is authorized in code (`src/server/domain/access.ts`, `viewer.ts`).
- Browser bundles contain only the Supabase URL and publishable key (checked by `test:ui` and by scanning `.next/static`).
- `audit_log` is append-only via triggers; a superuser/table owner can still change the trigger through DDL.
- The per-lease lock is a convention: any new code that changes payments, allocations or bills must call `lockLease()` first.

## Known limitations

- No UI to create leases, tenants or units (the lease API exists); no registration, password reset, or staff management.
- No rate limiting on login or the webhook; cookie-authenticated API calls do not refresh expired access tokens (page requests do, via `src/proxy.ts`).
- Money is displayed in MYR only; the dashboard is tables with simple bars (no charts or filters).
- Unapplied online funds are never auto-applied later (voiding another payment does not reallocate them).
- Some tests depend on the current Malaysia date (they build leases around "today") and the browser tests need Google Chrome installed.
- Local development stack only: nothing is configured for deployment; Supabase analytics and the edge runtime are disabled in `supabase/config.toml` to save memory.
- `ai-logs/` contains no transcripts yet; they must be exported manually (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## What would be implemented next

Lease/tenant/unit management screens, account self-service (password reset), rate limiting and webhook replay protection, a database-level balance guard (trigger) as a second layer under the lease lock, charts and filters on the dashboard, automatic application of unapplied online funds under a defined policy, and CI running the full suite.

# DECISIONS.md

> **TODO before submission:** two AI-log references in question 6 are placeholders (search for `PLACEHOLDER`). Export the AI session transcripts into `ai-logs/` (see `ai-logs/README.md`) and replace both placeholders with the real file name and turn/line. No log reference in this document has been invented.

Each answer is at most 150 words. Paths and line numbers refer to the repository as submitted (checked mechanically against the files).

## 1. Two `paid=true` callbacks arrive 5 ms apart

Both pass signature verification (`src/app/api/webhooks/gateway/route.ts:33`) and call `applyGatewayCallback` (`src/server/domain/gateway.ts:56`). The pre-lookup at `:66` only fetches the bill's lease id and decides nothing. Each opens a transaction (`:70`) whose first statement is `lockLease` (`:71`), a `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the lease row (`src/server/domain/payments.ts:16-17`). Callback A holds the lock; B waits. A re-reads the bill under the lock (`gateway.ts:72`), sees it unpaid, creates the single payment (`:89-91`) and marks the bill paid (`:96`). B resumes after A commits, re-reads (`:72`), sees `paid`, and returns at `:85` without writing. Backstop: `UNIQUE (gateway_bill_id)` (`supabase/migrations/20261020000100_schema.sql:118`), handled at `gateway.ts:102-105`. Proven by `tests/api/gateway.test.ts:370`.

## 2. Two staff record RM 800 and RM 700 concurrently, RM 1,000 remaining

Both requests resolve access (`src/server/domain/payments.ts:73`) and enter a transaction (`:86`). Its first statement, `lockLease` (`:87`, SQL at `:16-17`), is `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the lease row, so the second request waits. The winner (say RM 800) computes the maximum payable, remaining minus pending (`payments.ts:88-89`, `src/lib/allocation.ts:55`), which is RM 1,000; it passes the check at `payments.ts:90`, inserts a `pending_verification` payment (`payments.ts:92`) and commits. The loser then gets the lock, and `leaseState` now counts that payment in `pendingTotalSen` (`payments.ts:32`), so its maximum is RM 200 and RM 700 fails with HTTP 422 at `payments.ts:90`. The preventing lock is the PostgreSQL row lock on `public.leases`, shared by record, approve, reject, void and the webhook (`payments.ts:12-15`). Proven by `tests/api/concurrency-reports-slips.test.ts:19`.

## 3. Where code calculates "today" or converts between a calendar date and an instant

The business timezone is Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (UTC+8, no DST): due dates, overdue status and reports are Malaysian calendar concepts.

- Today / status: `src/lib/billing.ts:23,151-165`; `src/lib/malaysia.ts:9`, used at `src/server/domain/gateway.ts:19,25` and `src/server/domain/views.ts:76,112`.
- Gateway `paid_at` (+0800) → UTC: `malaysia.ts:18-27`, used at `gateway.ts:62`.
- Reports: `src/server/domain/reports.ts:16,28-33` (SQL `at time zone`).
- UI display/input: `src/lib/format-my.ts:25-44,59-60`; `src/components/lease/payment-form.tsx:41,63,102`.
- API instants need an explicit offset: `src/server/domain/convert.ts:20-23`.

Calendar dates have no timezone, so they map to UTC midnight: `convert.ts:16,18`, `scripts/seed.mts:108`, `src/lib/format.ts:59-60`; the picker uses local date parts (`src/lib/date.ts:13-22`). Instants are `timestamptz` (`schema.sql:109`).

## 4. Everything that bypasses RLS, and what enforces authorization

- **Prisma (database owner):** `src/server/prisma.ts:5,12`, reached through `getPrisma()` in every route and page. Authorization is explicit code: verified user (`src/server/http/auth.ts:24,37`, `src/server/http/session.ts:20`), then database roles from `src/server/domain/access.ts:23,26-35,37-44` and `viewer.ts:28-29`; role checks at `payments.ts:74,111,132,152`, `leases.ts:26-40`, `reports.ts:19-20,33`, `views.ts:42,68`, `gateway.ts:17-18,116`. The webhook relies on the HMAC (`route.ts:33`).
- **Service-role key:** `src/server/domain/slips.ts:57-59` (orphan-slip cleanup, own organization and unreferenced only, guarded by `src/app/actions/slips.ts:13-19`) and the seed (`scripts/seed.mts:70-79,139`).

-- EzyFusion core schema. Supabase SQL migrations are the ONLY source of schema changes (never Prisma Migrate).
--
-- Conventions
--   money            bigint, integer sen (never float / numeric)
--   calendar dates   date            (lease dates, period dates, due dates)
--   instants         timestamptz     (received_at, created_at)
--   tenancy          every org-owned row carries org_id; cross-organization references are made impossible
--                    by composite foreign keys (child_id, org_id) -> parent (id, org_id).
--   enumerations     text + CHECK (portable and easy to evolve in SQL migrations)

create extension if not exists btree_gist with schema extensions;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.organizations (
  id   uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null check (btrim(name) <> '')
);

create table public.memberships (
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  org_id  uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  role    text not null check (role in ('manager', 'staff')),
  primary key (user_id, org_id)
);
create index memberships_org_id_idx on public.memberships (org_id);

create table public.units (
  id     uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  name   text not null check (btrim(name) <> ''),
  unique (id, org_id),    -- target of composite foreign keys
  unique (org_id, name)
);

create table public.tenants (
  id        uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id    uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  user_id   uuid references auth.users (id) on delete set null,
  full_name text not null check (btrim(full_name) <> ''),
  email     text not null check (position('@' in email) > 1),
  phone     text check (phone is null or char_length(phone) between 1 and 32),
  unique (id, org_id),
  unique (org_id, email),
  unique (org_id, user_id)
);
create index tenants_user_id_idx on public.tenants (user_id);

create table public.leases (
  id               uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id           uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  unit_id          uuid not null,
  tenant_id        uuid not null,
  start_date       date not null,
  end_date         date not null,
  monthly_rent_sen bigint not null check (monthly_rent_sen > 0),
  deposit_sen      bigint not null default 0 check (deposit_sen >= 0),
  constraint leases_dates_check check (end_date >= start_date),
  constraint leases_unit_org_fk   foreign key (unit_id, org_id)   references public.units (id, org_id),
  constraint leases_tenant_org_fk foreign key (tenant_id, org_id) references public.tenants (id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id),
  -- a unit cannot be leased to two leases for overlapping (inclusive) date ranges
  constraint leases_unit_no_overlap exclude using gist (unit_id with =, daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') with &&)
);
create index leases_org_id_idx    on public.leases (org_id);
create index leases_tenant_id_idx on public.leases (tenant_id);
create index leases_unit_id_idx   on public.leases (unit_id);

create table public.invoices (
  id           uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id       uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  lease_id     uuid not null,
  kind         text not null check (kind in ('deposit', 'rent')),
  period_index integer,
  period_start date,
  period_end   date,
  due_date     date not null,
  amount_sen   bigint not null check (amount_sen >= 0),
  constraint invoices_lease_org_fk foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases (id, org_id),
  constraint invoices_kind_shape_check check (
    (kind = 'deposit' and period_index is null and period_start is null and period_end is null)
    or
    (kind = 'rent' and period_index >= 0 and period_start is not null and period_end is not null and period_end >= period_start)
  ),
  unique (id, org_id),
  unique (lease_id, period_index)              -- one rent invoice per period (deposit rows have NULL index)
);
create unique index invoices_one_deposit_per_lease on public.invoices (lease_id) where kind = 'deposit';
create index invoices_org_due_idx on public.invoices (org_id, due_date);

create table public.gateway_bills (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id     uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  lease_id   uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  status     text not null check (status in ('pending', 'paid', 'failed', 'expired')),
  constraint gateway_bills_lease_org_fk foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases (id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index gateway_bills_lease_id_idx on public.gateway_bills (lease_id);

create table public.payments (
  id              uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id          uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  lease_id        uuid not null,
  amount_sen      bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  unapplied_sen   bigint not null check (unapplied_sen >= 0),
  method          text not null check (method in ('cash', 'bank_transfer', 'gateway')),
  status          text not null check (status in ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected')),
  received_at     timestamptz not null,
  slip_path       text,
  gateway_bill_id uuid,
  constraint payments_unapplied_within_amount check (unapplied_sen <= amount_sen),
  -- slips live under "<org_id>/..." in the private payment-slips bucket
  constraint payments_slip_path_org_prefix check (slip_path is null or slip_path like org_id::text || '/%'),
  constraint payments_lease_org_fk        foreign key (lease_id, org_id)        references public.leases (id, org_id),
  constraint payments_gateway_bill_org_fk foreign key (gateway_bill_id, org_id) references public.gateway_bills (id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id),
  unique (gateway_bill_id)                       -- a bill settles at most one payment
);
create index payments_lease_id_idx on public.payments (lease_id);
create index payments_org_received_idx on public.payments (org_id, received_at);

create table public.payment_allocations (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id     uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  payment_id uuid not null,
  invoice_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  constraint payment_allocations_payment_org_fk foreign key (payment_id, org_id) references public.payments (id, org_id),
  constraint payment_allocations_invoice_org_fk foreign key (invoice_id, org_id) references public.invoices (id, org_id),
  unique (payment_id, invoice_id)
);
create index payment_allocations_invoice_id_idx on public.payment_allocations (invoice_id);

-- actor_id has no foreign key on purpose: audit rows must survive deletion of users (and the table is append-only).
create table public.audit_log (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id     uuid not null references public.organizations (id),
  actor_id   uuid,
  action     text not null check (btrim(action) <> ''),
  entity_id  uuid,
  details    jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index audit_log_org_created_idx on public.audit_log (org_id, created_at);

14	## Setup (exact commands)
15	
16	Prerequisites: Node.js 24, Docker Desktop running (at least ~8 GB memory allocated), free ports 54321-54324 and 3000.
17	
18	```bash
19	npx supabase start
20	npx supabase db reset
21	npm install
22	cp .env.example .env.local
23	npm run seed
24	npm run build && npm start
25	```
26	
27	Then open http://localhost:3000.
28	
29	Notes:
30	- `.env.example` already contains working **local-only** values (the Supabase CLI's well-known development defaults). No edits are needed for a local run. Get the live values any time with `npx supabase status -o env`.
31	- The first `supabase start` downloads about 8 GB of Docker images.
32	- If `npx supabase` runs before `npm install`, npx downloads the CLI on the fly (latest version). `npm install` first uses the version pinned in `package-lock.json`; both work with the migrations here.
33	- `npm install` runs `prisma generate` (postinstall); no database is needed for that.
34	- `npm run seed` is idempotent. For a pristine state run `npx supabase db reset` first.

65	## Features
66	
67	- **Billing rules** (`src/lib/billing.ts`): `generateSchedule`, `invoiceStatus`, `parseRinggitToSen` (integer sen, Malaysia time, month-end clamping, half-up proration).
68	- **Authentication:** email/password login, SSR session cookies, logout, role-aware navigation. Roles come from `memberships` and `tenants.user_id`, never from `user_metadata`. The API also accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
69	- **Staff / manager:** dashboard (overdue invoices, six-month collections), leases list and detail (invoices, payments, slip links), manual payment form (cash / bank transfer with slip upload), manager approve / reject / void.
70	- **Tenant:** own leases, invoices, payments, amount due now, "Pay now" (creates a gateway bill), return page, and phone-number update directly through the Data API (RLS + column grant).
71	- **Payments:** allocation by due date (deposit before rent, then period), payment cap (remaining balance minus pending), per-lease row lock for all money-changing operations, voiding.
72	- **Online payments:** `POST /api/leases/:id/gateway-bills`, signed webhook `POST /api/webhooks/gateway` (idempotent, concurrency-safe), `/payments/return` (read-only, never settles), simulator `node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false]`.
73	- **Database:** RLS on every public table, tenant/staff/manager policies, append-only `audit_log`, private `payment-slips` bucket with organization-scoped Storage policies.
74	
75	API: `POST /api/leases`, `GET /api/leases/:id`, `POST /api/leases/:id/payments`, `POST /api/leases/:id/gateway-bills`, `POST /api/payments/:id/approve|reject|void`, `GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM`, `POST /api/webhooks/gateway`.

77	## Tests
78	
79	The app and the Supabase stack must be running for the integration suites (`npm run build && npm start -- -p 3300`, `npx supabase start`, `npx supabase db reset`, `npm run seed`).
80	
81	| Command | What it runs |
82	|---|---|
83	| `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` | static checks and production build |
84	| `npm test` | unit tests (billing, allocation, signature, formatting) |
85	| `npm run test:tz` | the unit tests under `TZ=UTC`, `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur`, `America/New_York` |
86	| `npm run test:db` | schema, RLS, Storage and audit-log tests against the local database |
87	| `npm run test:api` | real HTTP tests incl. concurrency and the webhook (`API_BASE_URL`, default `http://localhost:3300`) |
88	| `npm run test:ui` | Chrome browser tests (`CHROME_PATH` to override `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/...`) |
89	| `npm run db:check` | Prisma schema vs. database consistency |
90	
91	Integration tests create and clean up their own leases/payments, but audit-log rows cannot be deleted: run `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed` for a pristine database.
92	
93	## Security notes
94	
95	- Prisma connects as the database owner and **bypasses RLS**: every server query is authorized in code (`src/server/domain/access.ts`, `viewer.ts`).
96	- Browser bundles contain only the Supabase URL and publishable key (checked by `test:ui` and by scanning `.next/static`).
97	- `audit_log` is append-only via triggers; a superuser/table owner can still change the trigger through DDL.
98	- The per-lease lock is a convention: any new code that changes payments, allocations or bills must call `lockLease()` first.
99	
100	## Known limitations
101	
102	- No UI to create leases, tenants or units (the lease API exists); no registration, password reset, or staff management.
103	- No rate limiting on login or the webhook; cookie-authenticated API calls do not refresh expired access tokens (page requests do, via `src/proxy.ts`).
104	- Money is displayed in MYR only; the dashboard is tables with simple bars (no charts or filters).
105	- Unapplied online funds are never auto-applied later (voiding another payment does not reallocate them).
106	- Some tests depend on the current Malaysia date (they build leases around "today") and the browser tests need Google Chrome installed.
107	- Local development stack only: nothing is configured for deployment; Supabase analytics and the edge runtime are disabled in `supabase/config.toml` to save memory.
108	- `ai-logs/` contains no transcripts yet; they must be exported manually (see `ai-logs/README.md`).
109	
110	## What would be implemented next
111	
112	Lease/tenant/unit management screens, account self-service (password reset), rate limiting and webhook replay protection, a database-level balance guard (trigger) as a second layer under the lease lock, charts and filters on the dashboard, automatic application of unapplied online funds under a defined policy, and CI running the full suite.

Available agent types for the Agent tool:
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)
- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Claude in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`), also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser: the user's real Chrome. Use it when the user asks for it by any of these names or by describing it.
A browser is unavailable only when none of its tools are in this session (neither loaded nor deferred) or its tool calls cannot reach the browser; a blocked site, a declined approval, or a sign-in page does not make a browser unavailable. If the user asks for one browser by name and it is unavailable, say so and ask before using the other one. When a sign-in page comes up, stay in that browser; if the user says they cannot sign in to a site in the built-in browser, offer Claude in Chrome and switch only if they agree.
</browsers>

<built_in_browser>
You have a built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser or the browser pane: a real browser with tabs inside the Claude desktop app, isolated from the user's Chrome, with its tools already loaded. You can use it for web research, reading pages and docs, checking staging or a deployed app, filling forms, and previewing this project's dev servers. `preview_start` with a `url` opens a site in its own tab; prefer `get_page_text` / `read_page` over screenshots for reading. The user sees the same pane and can take over; they may be asked to allow a site first, and if a site is refused or declined, tell them and move on rather than retrying. Treat any sign-ins there as the user's: never sign out, change credentials, or act on an account beyond what the task needs.
</built_in_browser>

<simulator_tools>
When the user wants to run, test, or visually check an iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?"), use mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control. Simulators and emulators only — when the user asks to run on their physical device ("on my phone", "on my device"), build for the device with your normal build tools instead; these tools and the panel cannot drive a real device. Open the live panel ('attach') whenever the user would want to see the app themselves — and call 'attach' FIRST, before you build or launch: it is cheap, it opens instantly on a booted device (and surfaces the one-time device-access prompt while the user is still at the keyboard), and if nothing is booted it returns a harmless, clear error — boot or build first in that case, then attach as soon as a device is up. Do not defer the panel to the implicit re-attach in 'launch'; the panel should already be open while you build. The panel is the user's view; your own verification (screenshot, tap, text) is headless and works without it — verify yourself rather than asking the user to check. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. An app in the iOS Simulator reaches a server on the machine your shell runs on at localhost, with no port forwarding.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
