name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

## Final report: **Not ready to submit yet** (code is ready; two document items need you)

### Fresh-run verification
I ran your exact commands in a clean copy, with no `node_modules`, `.next`, generated client or `.env.local`.
- `npx supabase start` and `npx supabase db reset` applied all 5 migrations.
- `npm install` and `cp .env.example .env.local` worked, and `npm run seed` produced the documented data.
  - **Seed counts:** 2 organizations, 3 memberships, 5 units, 4 tenants, 4 leases, 37 invoices, 2 payments, 3 allocations.
- `npm run build && npm start` served the app, and the seed password `Passw0rd!local` is documented in README.md and `.env.example`.
- `npx supabase` fetched CLI 2.121.0, which is the pinned version.

### Tests (all run against the fresh copy)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| lint | pass (exit 0) |
| typecheck | pass (exit 0) |
| build | pass |
| `db:check` | pass (10 models, 58 columns, 17 relations) |
| `test` | 98/98 |
| `test:tz` | 98/98 in each of the 3 timezones |
| `test:db` | 95/95 |
| `test:api` | 106/106 |
| `test:ui` | 21/21 |

### Security
- **Browser bundles:** none contain the secret key, `DATABASE_URL`, the gateway key or the seed password. The one `sb_secret_` match is supabase-js's own key-prefix check.
- **Anonymous access:** all 10 public tables return `42501` permission denied, and anonymous bucket listing is empty.
- **Database:** RLS is on for all 10 tables, and `payment-slips` is private.
- **Money columns:** every one is `bigint`, with no float or numeric columns.
- **Isolation and webhook:** the DB and API suites cover tenant and organization isolation, the return page not settling bills, and webhook idempotency under concurrency.
- **Git:** `.env.local` is ignored and `.env.example` is tracked (checked in a temporary copy). `billing.ts` and `billing.test.ts` still match their stored SHA-256 hashes.
- **Inventory:** all 10 required items exist.

### Blockers
1. **AI logs:** `ai-logs/` holds only an explanatory README, and no transcripts exist. DECISIONS.md Q6 has two `PLACEHOLDER` markers, flagged by a banner at the top. Export the session transcripts yourself, then replace both markers.
2. **REVIEW.md line numbers:** I mapped them from the ranges you gave (306–357, 360–399, 402–416) because I never had the original file. The mapping is stated at the top of REVIEW.md. Check a few against the original before submitting.

### Submission steps for you
1. Do the two blocker items above.
2. The workspace is not a git repo. Run `git init`, commit and push yourself (about 132 files would be tracked).
3. Submit through the portal.

### Known limitations (all listed in README.md)
- No UI to create leases, tenants or units.
- No rate limiting.
- Some tests depend on today's Malaysia date.
- UI tests need Chrome.

Reset note: the local Supabase stack is now running from the scratch copy, which uses the same project id as the real one. Run `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed` in the project folder when you want a clean state.

EzyFusion — Dark Premium SaaS UI Redesign
Project: ~/ezyfusion-assessment
You are a senior product designer and frontend engineer specializing in premium fintech and property management SaaS applications.
Redesign the existing Next.js application into a cohesive, production-quality Dark Premium Dashboard.
This is a visual and UX redesign, NOT a backend rewrite.
1. Mandatory constraints

* Preserve all existing business logic, API contracts, database schema, Supabase authentication, RLS, payments, gateway webhook, allocation and timezone behavior.
* Use the existing Next.js 16 App Router, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui components.
* Keep the application fully functional with real data.
* Do not introduce mock dashboard data.
* Do not modify billing.ts or its tests.
* Do not remove existing features.
* Do not commit, push or deploy.
* Respect the assessment deadline; avoid unnecessary dependencies and complex animations.

2. Visual direction
Style: Dark Premium Fintech SaaS.
The interface should feel like a polished commercial product, not a generic shadcn starter template.
Design tokens:
Background: #090E1A
Sidebar: #0D1422
Surface: #121B2B
Elevated Surface: #192438
Border: #263348
Primary: #818CF8
Primary Hover: #6366F1
Success: #34D399
Warning: #FBBF24
Danger: #FB7185
Primary Text: #F1F5F9
Secondary Text: #94A3B8
Muted Text: #64748B
Use CSS variables and semantic Tailwind tokens rather than scattering hardcoded colors.
Typography:

* Inter or Geist
* Clear headings and hierarchy
* Tabular numerals for financial values
* Consistent font sizes and weights

Spacing:

* 8px spacing system
* Comfortable 20–24px card padding
* Consistent 12–16px component gaps
* Rounded corners 12–16px
* Subtle borders and restrained shadows

Avoid:

* Excessive gradients
* Neon effects
* Glassmorphism everywhere
* Huge empty cards
* Unnecessary animations
* Low-contrast gray text
* Generic dashboard placeholder content

3. Application shell
Build a unified application shell:
Desktop:

* Fixed/collapsible sidebar, approximately 260px
* Product branding
* Role-aware navigation
* Active route indication
* Top header with page title, breadcrumb and account controls
* Consistent content width and padding

Mobile:

* Accessible navigation drawer
* Compact header
* No horizontal page overflow
* Tables may scroll within their containers

Navigation must respect actual permissions.
4. Dashboard
Redesign /dashboard with:

* Strong page heading and supporting description
* Summary cards for overdue invoices and payments awaiting verification
* Collections visualization for the last six Malaysia calendar months
* Clear RM currency formatting
* Meaningful empty states
* Elegant loading skeletons

Charts must use actual collections data. Prefer lightweight existing dependencies or CSS/SVG instead of adding a heavy chart library.
5. Leases
Redesign /leases:

* Professional data table
* Strong typography hierarchy
* Clear status badges
* Well-aligned currency columns
* Responsive layout
* Helpful empty states

Redesign /leases/[id]:

* Lease overview header
* Financial summary
* Invoices table
* Payment history
* Manual payment form
* Manager approval, rejection and void actions

Organize the information into distinct, readable sections.
Do not alter payment validation or authorization.
6. Payment UX
Improve the existing payment form:

* Clear field labels
* Inline validation
* Distinct payment methods
* Upload area for bank transfer slips
* Loading states
* Success and error toasts
* Accessible confirmation dialogs

Payment statuses should be immediately understandable.
Preserve existing API calls and behavior.
7. Tenant portal
Redesign /portal and /portal/leases/[id]:

* Premium tenant-facing layout
* Lease summary cards
* Outstanding balance prominently displayed
* Invoice history
* Payment history
* Clear Pay Now primary action
* Gateway bill confirmation
* Phone editing form

The Pay Now action must only create a bill, never mark it paid.
Redesign /payments/return using the same design system. Display only the database-backed bill status.
8. Authentication
Redesign /login:

* Premium split-screen desktop layout
* Product branding and short value proposition
* Elegant login form
* Strong mobile layout
* Accessible errors and loading states

Do not change authentication semantics or expose secrets.
9. Components and interaction
Build or refine reusable components:

* PageHeader
* StatCard
* SectionCard
* DataTable styling
* StatusBadge
* EmptyState
* LoadingSkeleton
* ConfirmationDialog
* FormField

Use accessible focus states, keyboard navigation, readable contrast and consistent hover/disabled states.
10. Implementation workflow
First inspect the existing application structure, CSS variables, components and routes.
Then implement the design system and shared shell.
Then update all existing pages.
Do not stop after changing colors. The layout, information hierarchy, forms, tables and responsive behavior must also improve.
Keep all existing business flows operational.
11. Verification
Run:

* npm run lint
* npm run typecheck
* npm run build
* npm run test
* npm run test
* npm run test
* npm run test

Use browser screenshots at desktop (1440px) and mobile (390px) to visually inspect:

* Login
* Dashboard
* Leases
* Lease details
* Tenant portal
* Tenant lease details
* Payment return

Check for clipping, overflow, poor contrast, broken navigation and hydration warnings.
Do not claim visual verification unless screenshots were actually inspected.
Final report
Provide:

1. Design system changes
2. Pages redesigned
3. Components created or updated
4. Screenshots captured and inspected
5. Test results
6. Any remaining UI issues

Do not commit or deploy.
</pasted_content id="a84f">

content.text:
The dark premium redesign is done across all pages, and every check passes. Backend, API contracts, schema, auth, RLS, payments, webhook and allocation are untouched. `billing.ts` and its tests are byte-identical, and nothing was committed or deployed.

## 1. Design system changes
- **Palette:** `src/app/globals.css` now holds your palette as CSS variables (background `#090E1A`, sidebar `#0D1422`, surface `#121B2B`, elevated `#192438`, border `#263348`, primary `#818CF8` with hover `#6366F1`). Success, warning, danger and the three text levels use your values too. Everything downstream uses semantic Tailwind tokens, so no colours are hardcoded in pages.
- **Muted text:** `#64748B` is below 4.5:1 contrast on the surfaces, so I used it only for placeholders and icons. Body secondary text is `#94A3B8`, and `#A9B6C9` where it needs more prominence.
- **Sizing and type:** radius is 10/12/16px, card padding 20px, and financial figures use tabular numerals through a new `num` utility. Geist is kept.
- **Primitives restyled for dark:** button (new `sm` and `lg` sizes), card, table (uppercase muted headers, 44px header row), dialog and sheet overlays, toaster, textarea and inputs.
- **Button link fix:** `buttonVariants` is now class-merged. Link-styled buttons were losing their outline border before.

## 2. Pages redesigned
- **Login:** split-screen on desktop with branding and three real feature points; stacked on mobile.
- **App shell:** collapsible 260px sidebar, header with breadcrumb and account controls, mobile drawer.
- **Staff pages:** dashboard, `/leases` and `/leases/[id]`.
- **Tenant pages:** `/portal`, `/portal/leases/[id]` and `/payments/return`.

**Dashboard:** the chart is drawn from the real six-month collections with plain elements, no library. The data table is kept beside it for accessibility and tests.

**Lease details:** a financial summary row, an overview block, then invoices, payments and the payment form as separate sections.

**Tenant lease page:** the outstanding balance and Pay now are the top card. The page still reads only the database-backed bill status; I loaded the return page with `paid=true` and it still showed Pending.

## 3. Components created or updated
- **New:** `StatCard`, `SectionCard`, `LoadingSkeleton`, `FormField` and `ConfirmationDialog` (it replaces the old reason dialog, with the same behaviour).
- **Updated:** `PageHeader`, `StatusBadge`, `EmptyState`, `AppShell`, `NavLinks`, `Breadcrumb`, `PaymentForm`, `PayNow`, `PhoneForm` and `LoginForm`.
- **Payment form:** a slip dropzone, an "RM" prefix on the amount, inline errors, a loading state and toasts. The method is still a dropdown; I did not change it to radio cards because the UI tests drive `#pay-method` as a select.
- **Route layout:** the signed-in pages moved into a `(shell)` route group with its own layout, so `/login` renders without the sidebar. URLs are unchanged.

## 4. Screenshots captured and inspected
I inspected these in the built-in browser, with real data created through the UI:
- **1440px:** login, dashboard (with chart data), leases, lease details with the payment form and its validation error, the void dialog, tenant portal, tenant lease details, payment return.
- **390px:** login, dashboard, chart, lease details, payments table, mobile drawer, tenant portal, tenant lease with the bill-created state, payment return.
- **Overflow:** no horizontal page overflow at 390px (`scrollWidth` equalled `innerWidth`). Tables scroll inside their own containers.
- **Mobile bug found and fixed:** the chart's month labels collided at 390px. They now show the month only.
- **Not screenshotted:** the pending-payment approve/reject dialog (no pending payment existed) and the mobile leases list.

## 5. Test results
- `lint`, `typecheck` and `build` all passed.
- `npm test` passed 98/98, and `test:tz` passed 98/98 in each of the 3 timezones.
- `db:check` passed.
- `test:db` passed 95/95 on a freshly reset and seeded database.
- `test:api` passed 106/106 and `test:ui` passed 21/21.
- The UI suite watches the console for errors and warnings during its flows, and none were recorded. The browser pane's console showed nothing either, but I did not run a dev-mode hydration check.
- The `test:db` suite asserts absolute seed counts, so after the API and UI runs it fails until you run `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed` again. It failed once for exactly that reason before I reset.

## 6. Remaining UI issues
- Approve is still one click, because the existing UI tests expect that. Reject and void use the confirmation dialog.
- The sidebar collapse state is not remembered between page loads.
- Chart bar labels show whole ringgit when the amount is exact and cents otherwise.
- The stat cards are fairly tall on mobile.
- The README's dashboard limitation and theme notes were updated to match the redesign.

The local database currently contains test-run data from the API and UI suites. Run `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed` for a clean state before submitting.

Muted text: #64748B is below 4.5:1 contrast on the surfaces, so I used it only for placeholders and icons. Body secondary text is #94A3B8, and #A9B6C9 where it needs more prominence.
Sizing and type: radius is 10/12/16px, card padding 20px, and financial figures use tabular numerals through a new num utility. Geist is kept.
Primitives restyled for dark: button (new sm and lg sizes), card, table (uppercase muted headers, 44px header row), dialog and sheet overlays, toaster, textarea and inputs.
Button link fix: buttonVariants is now class-merged. Link-styled buttons were losing their outline border before.
2. Pages redesigned
Login: split-screen on desktop with branding and three real feature points; stacked on mobile.
App shell: collapsible 260px sidebar, header with breadcrumb and account controls, mobile drawer.
Staff pages: dashboard, /leases and /leases/[id].
Tenant pages: /portal, /portal/leases/[id] and /payments/return.
Dashboard: the chart is drawn from the real six-month collections with plain elements, no library. The data table is kept beside it for accessibility and tests.

Lease details: a financial summary row, an overview block, then invoices, payments and the payment form as separate sections.

Tenant lease page: the outstanding balance and Pay now are the top card. The page still reads only the database-backed bill status; I loaded the return page with paid=true and it still showed Pending.

3. Components created or updated
New: StatCard, SectionCard, LoadingSkeleton, FormField and ConfirmationDialog (it replaces the old reason dialog, with the same behaviour).
Updated: PageHeader, StatusBadge, EmptyState, AppShell, NavLinks, Breadcrumb, PaymentForm, PayNow, PhoneForm and LoginForm.
Payment form: a slip dropzone, an “RM” prefix on the amount, inline errors, a loading state and toasts. The method is still a dropdown; I did not change it to radio cards because the UI tests drive #pay-method as a select.
Route layout: the signed-in pages moved into a (shell) route group with its own layout, so /login renders without the sidebar. URLs are unchanged.
4. Screenshots captured and inspected
I inspected these in the built-in browser, with real data created through the UI:

1440px: login, dashboard (with chart data), leases, lease details with the payment form and its validation error, the void dialog, tenant portal, tenant lease details, payment return.
390px: login, dashboard, chart, lease details, payments table, mobile drawer, tenant portal, tenant lease with the bill-created state, payment return.
Overflow: no horizontal page overflow at 390px (scrollWidth equalled innerWidth). Tables scroll inside their own containers.
Mobile bug found and fixed: the chart’s month labels collided at 390px. They now show the month only.
Not screenshotted: the pending-payment approve/reject dialog (no pending payment existed) and the mobile leases list.
5. Test results
lint, typecheck and build all passed.
npm test passed 98/98, and test:tz passed 98/98 in each of the 3 timezones.
db:check passed.
test:db passed 95/95 on a freshly reset and seeded database.
test:api passed 106/106 and test:ui passed 21/21.
The UI suite watches the console for errors and warnings during its flows, and none were recorded. The browser pane’s console showed nothing either, but I did not run a dev-mode hydration check.
The test:db suite asserts absolute seed counts, so after the API and UI runs it fails until you run npx supabase db reset && npm run seed again. It failed once for exactly that reason before I reset.
6. Remaining UI issues
Approve is still one click, because the existing UI tests expect that. Reject and void use the confirmation dialog.
The sidebar collapse state is not remembered between page loads.
Chart bar labels show whole ringgit when the amount is exact and cents otherwise.
The stat cards are fairly tall on mobile.
The README’s dashboard limitation and theme notes were updated to match the redesign.
The local database currently contains test-run data from the API and UI suites. Run npx supabase db reset && npm run seed for a clean state before submittin

content.text:
I fixed the Next.js issues. The overlay was reporting "Blocking Route: `Date.now()` while prerendering" on the signed-in pages. It showed 2 issues when I opened it, and the dev log had the same error for `/`, `/dashboard`, `/leases`, `/leases/[id]`, `/portal`, `/portal/leases/[id]` and `/payments/return`. I did not see the count of 4 myself.

**Cause:** the session lookup in [session.ts](src/server/http/session.ts) (token check and database read) was running during Next's prerender and prefetch passes, where reading the clock is flagged.

**Fix:** I added `await connection()` at the top of `sessionUser`, which is what Next's own error message suggests. That makes the lookup request-time only. It is a one-line change plus a comment, and no business logic changed.

**Checked:** after the fix I loaded `/`, `/dashboard`, `/leases` and a lease detail page in your dev server on port 3000, signed in as the manager. The issues badge is gone and the dev log shows no new errors since the change. I did not reload the tenant pages or `/payments/return` after the fix, but they use the same session lookup.

Lint, typecheck and the build pass. `test:api` passes 106/106 and `test:ui` passes 21/21. I did not re-run the unit and DB suites, since this change doesn't touch them.

I did not run the database reset you declined. The data currently in the database is whatever it was when I started, and it was already different from my last run (the dashboard showed RM 2,000.00 collected, not RM 2,050.50). `test:db` asserts the pristine seed counts, so run `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed` yourself when you want that state.

async function onSubmit(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault()
    if (submitting) return
    setFormError(null)
    const next: Errors = {}
    if (!unitId) next.unit = 'Select a unit.'
    if (!tenantId) next.tenant = 'Select a tenant.'

content.text:
The Create Lease UI works end to end. Lint, typecheck, build, unit and UI tests pass, and all lease creation and options API tests pass. One older API test fails because of leftover data in the local database.

## What it does
- **Button:** `/leases` shows "Create lease" only to managers. Staff never see it, and staff, tenants and anonymous users cannot use the page or the options endpoint.
- **Form:** `/leases/new` is a responsive form with Unit, Tenant, Start date, End date, Monthly rent and Deposit.
- **API contract:** I read `POST /api/leases` and `createLease` first. The form sends `unitId`, `tenantId`, `startDate`, `endDate` and integer `monthlyRentSen` and `depositSen`, as the API expects.
- **Money and dates:** ringgit is parsed with the existing `parseRinggitToSen`. Dates are plain `YYYY-MM-DD` strings, so Malaysia calendar semantics are unchanged.
- **Submission:** it goes through the existing `postJson` client. Validation and conflict messages from the API are shown in an alert and a toast. Success redirects to the new lease's detail page.
- **Unit choices:** the unit list shows the date ranges already leased, as a hint. The database exclusion constraint still decides overlaps, and an overlap returns the existing 409 message.
- **Tenant isolation:** a multi-organization manager also gets an Organization selector.

## Backend added
No safe read endpoint existed, so I added one read-only, manager-only, organization-scoped endpoint, `GET /api/leases/options`. It reuses the same authentication and `orgIdsWithRole` check as `POST /api/leases`.

I did not touch `billing.ts` (hash identical), the migrations, payment logic or webhook code.

## Files changed
**New**
- `src/app/(shell)/(staff)/leases/new/page.tsx`

<pasted_content id="a84f">
Test Requirements
Technical Assessment - Rent Collection
Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router) - TypeScript - Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Storage) - Prisma - shadcn/ui - Tailwind CSS

Time: the timer above is what counts, normally 4 hours (about 30 min reading - 3 h building - 30 min write-ups and submission)

Read This First
AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot...) are allowed and expected. We assess whether you understand and control what gets built. Code you cannot explain counts as not done.

Hidden tests. We run automated tests against every rule in this brief, including edge cases that are not in the examples:
your billing functions, about 50 hidden cases, run under TZ=UTC, TZ=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur and TZ=America/New_York
your HTTP API, called as each seeded account, including requests about other organizations' records and concurrent requests
your Supabase Data API and Storage bucket, called directly with your publishable key and each user's token
your payment webhook, with valid, forged, duplicated, concurrent and out-of-order callbacks
AI logs. Export the transcript of every AI session you use (in Claude Code: /export) into an ai-logs/ folder in your repo. We do not count how much you used AI. We look at how you directed it, what you checked and what you corrected.
Walkthrough. If your submission passes, the interview starts with a 30-minute walkthrough of your code: we pick parts of it, ask "what happens if...", and ask you to make a small change live.
Priorities. A correct and secure subset beats a complete but sloppy app. If time runs short, work in this order: billing functions (section 3), access control (6), payments (4), webhook (5), UI (9). Say in your README what you skipped.
Names are a contract. Table names, column names, endpoint paths, file paths and response shapes in this brief are what our tests use. You may add more of your own.
1. The Business
You are building part of the rent collection module of a property management platform used by Malaysian property management companies.

Each organization (a property management company) rents units to tenants under leases.
A lease produces invoices: an optional deposit, plus one rent invoice per monthly period.
Tenants pay by cash, by bank transfer (with an uploaded slip), or online through a payment gateway. Payments are allocated to invoices.
Business timezone: Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (UTC+8, no daylight saving). Currency: MYR (RM). 1 ringgit = 100 sen.
Your server runs in UTC and our assessors work from several timezones. Every date and time the app shows or accepts is Malaysia time, whatever the timezone of the server or of the viewer's device.
Roles
Role	Who	Can
manager	Organization admin	Everything in their organization: create leases, record payments (approved immediately), approve, reject and void payments, read the audit log
staff	Front desk	Read their organization's leases, invoices and payments; record payments (these wait for a manager's approval)
tenant	Renter	Read their own profile, leases, invoices and payments; update their own phone number; pay online
A staff member or manager belongs to exactly one organization. Nobody ever sees another organization's data.

2. Local Setup and Seed Data
Develop against a local Supabase stack (Docker and the Supabase CLI), not a cloud project. See Supabase local development. We grade by running your project on our machine from a fresh clone, with exactly these commands:

npx supabase start            # starts the stack from your supabase/config.toml
npx supabase db reset         # rebuilds the database from supabase/migrations/
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local    # we replace keys with the values from `npx supabase status` if they differ
npm run seed
npm run build && npm start
Commit supabase/config.toml, supabase/migrations/, and an .env.example that lists every variable your app needs, with local values and a comment saying where each one comes from.
npm run seed creates exactly the data below on a freshly reset database, through your normal code paths (your lease creation and payment logic), so the invoices and allocations it produces are the ones your app would produce.
All seeded accounts share one password of your choice, which you submit with your work.
Organizations and accounts
Organization	Account	Role	Notes
Northwind Properties	manager@northwind.test	manager	
Northwind Properties	staff@northwind.test	staff	
Northwind Properties	aisyah@northwind.test	tenant	Tenant "Aisyah Rahman"
Northwind Properties	ben@northwind.test	tenant	Tenant "Ben Lim"
Northwind Properties	probe@northwind.test	tenant	Tenant "Probe Tenant" (our tests create payments and leases for this tenant)
Beta Realty	manager@beta.test	manager	
Beta Realty	chen@beta.test	tenant	Tenant "Chen Wei"
Units and leases
Organization	Unit	Tenant	Start	End	Monthly rent	Deposit
Northwind	A-12-3	Aisyah Rahman	2026-01-31	2026-07-15	RM 1,500.00	RM 3,000.00
Northwind	B-05-1	Ben Lim	2026-01-01	2026-04-15	RM 1,000.29	none
Northwind	C-01-7	Probe Tenant	2026-02-28	2027-02-27	RM 2,000.00	RM 4,000.00
Northwind	D-03-2	(no lease)				
Beta	KL-1	Chen Wei	2026-03-15	2027-03-14	RM 2,200.00	RM 4,400.00
Payments on Aisyah's lease
Cash, RM 3,000.00, received 2026-01-31 10:00 Malaysia time, recorded by the manager.
Bank transfer, RM 2,000.00, received 2026-03-01 00:30 Malaysia time, recorded by staff with a slip file, then approved by the manager.
3. Billing Rules - lib/billing.ts
Create lib/billing.ts (or src/lib/billing.ts). It must be pure: no I/O, no imports from Next.js, React, Supabase or Prisma, and no dependence on the timezone of the machine it runs on. Your app must use it, and we test it directly.

export type InvoiceKind = 'deposit' | 'rent'
 
export interface ScheduledInvoice {
  kind: InvoiceKind
  periodIndex: number | null  // 0, 1, 2... for rent; null for the deposit
  periodStart: string | null  // 'YYYY-MM-DD'; null for the deposit
  periodEnd: string | null    // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive; null for the deposit
  dueDate: string             // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
  amountSen: number           // integer
}
 
export function generateSchedule(lease: {
  startDate: string           // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
  endDate: string             // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive (the tenant's last day)
  monthlyRentSen: number
  depositSen: number
}): ScheduledInvoice[]
 
export type InvoiceStatus = 'paid' | 'partially_paid' | 'unpaid' | 'overdue'
 
export function invoiceStatus(
  invoice: { dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number },
  now: Date,
): InvoiceStatus
 
export function parseRinggitToSen(input: string): number
generateSchedule
Validation. Throw an Error if a date is not a real calendar date written as YYYY-MM-DD, if endDate is before startDate, if monthlyRentSen is not a positive integer, or if depositSen is not a non-negative integer.
Deposit. If depositSen > 0, the first invoice is the deposit: kind: 'deposit', due on startDate, period fields null.
Anchors. Rent periods are anchored on the start date. The anchor of period k is the start date plus k calendar months, always counted from the start date (never from the previous anchor). If that month has fewer days than the start day, use the month's last day. A lease starting on Jan 31 has anchors Jan 31, Feb 28 (Feb 29 in leap years), Mar 31, Apr 30, and so on.
Periods. Period k runs from anchor k to the day before anchor k+1, and is due on anchor k. There is a period for every anchor on or before endDate.
Last period. It is cut at endDate. If it is shorter than its full length, it costs monthlyRentSen x days used / days in the full period, rounded half up to the nearest sen. Every other period costs monthlyRentSen.
Order. The deposit first, then rent by period index.
Worked example (Aisyah's lease):

Period	Kind	Dates	Due	Amount
deposit		2026-01-31	RM 3,000.00
0	rent	2026-01-31 to 2026-02-27	2026-01-31	RM 1,500.00
1	rent	2026-02-28 to 2026-03-30	2026-02-28	RM 1,500.00
2	rent	2026-03-31 to 2026-04-29	2026-03-31	RM 1,500.00
3	rent	2026-04-30 to 2026-05-30	2026-04-30	RM 1,500.00
4	rent	2026-05-31 to 2026-06-29	2026-05-31	RM 1,500.00
5	rent	2026-06-30 to 2026-07-15	2026-06-30	RM 774.19
Period 5 uses 16 of the 31 days from 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-30: 150000 x 16 / 31 = 77419.35, so 77419 sen.

invoiceStatus
Apply these rules in order:

paid if paidSen >= amountSen.
overdue if today's Malaysia date is after dueDate. An invoice due 2026-03-01 becomes overdue at 2026-03-02 00:00 Malaysia time (2026-03-01T16:00:00Z), not a moment earlier.
partially_paid if paidSen > 0.
Otherwise unpaid.
parseRinggitToSen
Turns what a user types into sen. It accepts digits with optional comma thousands separators (groups of exactly three digits) and an optional decimal part of one or two digits, ignoring whitespace around the value: "1,500.50" gives 150050, "1.15" gives 115, "7" gives 700. Anything else throws an Error, for example "", "-5", "1.234", "1e3", "RM 10", "1,23".

4. Payments
Recording a payment
Staff and managers record cash or bank transfer payments on a lease: the amount, the method, and the date and time the money was received (entered and shown in Malaysia time).
A bank transfer needs a slip: a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 5 MB, stored in Supabase Storage (section 6). If recording fails after the upload, the file must not be left behind.
A payment recorded by a manager is approved immediately. A payment recorded by staff is pending_verification until a manager approves or rejects it.
Cap. A new payment may not be more than the lease's remaining balance (the total of all its invoices minus everything allocated to them) minus the total of the lease's payments still pending_verification. Paying future periods in advance is allowed within the cap.
Approving, rejecting and voiding (managers only)
Approve a pending_verification payment. At that moment, check again that it is not more than the lease's remaining balance. If it is, refuse and leave it pending.
Reject a pending_verification payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters.
Void an approved payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters. Voiding removes that payment's allocations. Other payments' allocations do not change.
Payments are never deleted. Every approval, rejection, void and lease creation writes a row to audit_log (who, what, when, details).
Allocation
When a payment becomes approved, its amount is allocated to the lease's invoices that still have something unpaid, in this order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index. Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one, including invoices that are not due yet. Whatever is left once every invoice is fully paid is stored on the payment as unapplied_sen. Only online payments can end up with an unapplied amount, because manual payments are capped.

The paid amount of an invoice is the sum of its allocations. Statuses are computed with invoiceStatus, never stored.

All of this must stay correct when requests arrive at the same time. For example, two staff members recording payments on the same lease at once must not exceed the cap together, and a payment approved twice at once is allocated once.

Collections report
The total of approved payments for each calendar month of received_at in Malaysia time, over a range of months, including months with nothing collected. With the seed data, Northwind's report for 2026-01 to 2026-03 is [{ month: '2026-01', collectedSen: 300000 }, { month: '2026-02', collectedSen: 0 }, { month: '2026-03', collectedSen: 200000 }].

5. Online Payments
A tenant pays online like this:

The tenant clicks Pay now on their lease. Your API creates a gateway bill for the amount due now: the unpaid amounts of the lease's invoices due on or before today's Malaysia date. If nothing is due, refuse. Bill ids must be impossible to guess.
In production the tenant would now be redirected to the gateway. In this test, show the bill id and amount: we play the gateway using the simulator below.
The gateway calls your webhook, POST /api/webhooks/gateway. Only the webhook can settle a bill. The gateway also sends the tenant back to /payments/return?bill_id=...&paid=true. That page only shows the bill's real status from your database and changes nothing.
Webhook
The request body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with these fields. The gateway may add more fields in future.

Field	Example	Notes
id	bill_8f3a2c	Your bill id (this short example is guessable; yours must not be)
paid	true	true or false
paid_amount	210050	Amount in sen; 0 when not paid
paid_at	2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800	When it was paid
transaction_id	TX-000123	Gateway transaction id
transaction_status	completed	completed, failed or pending
x_signature	06994f...	See below
Signature. Take every field in the request except x_signature, sort them by key (ascending by character code), write each one as the key immediately followed by the value, join them with |, and compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the resulting string with your secret key GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY, as lowercase hex. Test vector, with the key test_x_signature_key and the six example values above:

source:    idbill_8f3a2c|paidtrue|paid_amount210050|paid_at2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800|transaction_idTX-000123|transaction_statuscompleted
signature: 06994fab2d674e7829144eaa2204631716d3c099b503d38945e92b6296531641
Required behavior:

Situation	Response	Effect
Signature missing or wrong	401	None
Unknown bill id	404	None
paid=true and paid_amount is not the bill's amount	422	None
paid=true, bill pending or failed	200	Bill becomes paid, and one approved online payment is created with received_at = paid_at, then allocated
paid=true, bill already paid (a repeat delivery)	200	None
paid=false, bill pending	200	Bill becomes failed
paid=false, bill already failed (a repeat delivery)	200	None
paid=false, bill already paid (late or out of order)	200	None: a paid bill never goes back
The gateway retries, so it may deliver the same callback several times, including at the same moment. A bill creates at most one payment, ever. Never log the secret key or whole callback payloads.

Simulator
Save this as gateway-sim.mjs and run node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false] with GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY set.

import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'
 
const [billId, amountSen, paid = 'true'] = process.argv.slice(2)
const url = process.env.WEBHOOK_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway'
const key = process.env.GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY
 
const myt = new Date(Date.now() + 8 * 3600 * 1000).toISOString()
const fields = {
  id: billId,
  paid,
  paid_amount: paid === 'true' ? amountSen : '0',
  paid_at: `${myt.slice(0, 10)} ${myt.slice(11, 19)} +0800`,
  transaction_id: `TX-${Date.now()}`,
  transaction_status: paid === 'true' ? 'completed' : 'failed',
}
const source = Object.keys(fields).sort().map(k => `${k}${fields[k]}`).join('|')
fields.x_signature = createHmac('sha256', key).update(source).digest('hex')
 
const res = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
  body: new URLSearchParams(fields),
})
console.log(res.status, await res.text())
6. Access Control
Access is enforced in two places, and we test both:

Your server code: route handlers, Server Actions and server components. Every endpoint must authenticate the caller and check their organization and role itself. A protected page or a hidden button is not a check.
The Supabase Data API and Storage, which anyone holding your publishable key can call directly with their own access token.
Server code
Roles come from your memberships table, and from tenants.user_id for tenants. Never take a role or an organization from anything the user can edit, such as user_metadata.
On the server, authenticate with supabase.auth.getUser() or getClaims(), not getSession().
A request about a record in another organization, or another tenant's record, gets 404: do not reveal that it exists. A request about a record the caller can see, for an action their role does not allow, gets 403. A request without a valid login gets 401.
IDs in request bodies are untrusted too. For example, a manager must not be able to create a lease on another organization's unit or tenant.
Our tests call your API with Authorization: Bearer <access token>, where the token is a Supabase access token for one of the seeded users. Accept that header as well as the normal session cookie.
The service role (secret) key must never reach the browser.
Data API
This table is the most access allowed through the Supabase Data API, which is PostgREST called with a user's token. Granting less is fine where your app does not need it, with one exception: the tenant portal reads the tenant's own data, and updates their phone number, directly from the browser with supabase-js.

Table	anon	tenant	staff	manager
organizations	none	read own organization	read own organization	read own organization
memberships	none	none	read own organization	read own organization
units	none	read the units of own leases	read own organization	read own organization
tenants	none	read own row, update only phone	read own organization	read own organization
leases, invoices, payments, payment_allocations, gateway_bills	none	read the rows of own leases	read own organization	read own organization
audit_log	none	none	none	read own organization
Every other insert, update or delete through the Data API must fail for everyone. This covers every table, view and function (/rest/v1/rpc/...) you create, not just the ones above. audit_log is append-only for every role, including the service role and the database owner.

Storage
Bank transfer slips go in a private bucket named payment-slips, under <org_id>/.... Only staff and managers of that organization can upload there, and they read slips through short-lived signed URLs. Tenants, other organizations and anonymous users cannot read, list or upload slips. A payment's slip_path must point to an existing file in its own organization's folder.

7. HTTP API
Request and response bodies are JSON, except for the webhook. Amounts are integers in sen. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and instants are ISO 8601 with an offset. Errors return { "error": "message" }.

Method and path	Who	Success	Other responses
POST /api/leases	manager	201 { id }	400 invalid input, 409 overlaps another lease on the unit
GET /api/leases/:leaseId	staff, manager, the lease's tenant	200, shape below	
POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments	staff, manager	201 { id, status }	400 invalid input, 422 over the cap
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/approve	manager	200 { status }	409 not pending, 422 over the remaining balance
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject	manager	200 { status }	400 missing reason, 409 not pending
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void	manager	200 { status }	400 missing reason, 409 not approved
POST /api/leases/:leaseId/gateway-bills	the lease's tenant	201 { billId, amountSen }	422 nothing due
GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM	staff, manager	200 [{ month: 'YYYY-MM', collectedSen }], one entry per month in order	400 invalid range
POST /api/webhooks/gateway	the gateway	see section 5	
Every endpoint also returns 401, 403 and 404 as described in section 6. Request bodies:

// POST /api/leases
{ unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
 
// POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments
{ amountSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer'; receivedAt: string; slipPath?: string }
 
// POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject and POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void
{ reason: string }
GET /api/leases/:leaseId returns the invoices in allocation order:

{
  lease: { id: string; unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
  invoices: {
    id: string; kind: 'deposit' | 'rent'; periodIndex: number | null; periodStart: string | null; periodEnd: string | null
    dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number; status: InvoiceStatus
  }[]
  payments: {
    id: string; amountSen: number; unappliedSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer' | 'online'
    status: 'pending_verification' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'voided'; receivedAt: string
  }[]
}
Creating a lease stores the lease and exactly the invoices generateSchedule returns, all or nothing. Leases on the same unit never overlap (both dates are inclusive), even when two requests arrive at the same moment.

8. Database
Keep every database object in SQL migrations under supabase/migrations/: tables, constraints, RLS policies, grants, functions, triggers, and the storage bucket and its policies. npx supabase db reset must rebuild all of it; nothing may depend on changes made by hand in Supabase Studio. Use Prisma for server-side data access, with prisma/schema.prisma matching the database.
Store money as integer sen (bigint), never as a floating-point type. Calendar dates are date, and instants are timestamptz.
Required tables and columns (add whatever else you need):
Table	Required columns
organizations	id, name
memberships	user_id, org_id, role (manager or staff)
units	id, org_id, name
tenants	id, org_id, user_id, full_name, email, phone
leases	id, org_id, unit_id, tenant_id, start_date, end_date, monthly_rent_sen, deposit_sen
invoices	id, org_id, lease_id, kind, period_index, period_start, period_end, due_date, amount_sen
payments	id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, unapplied_sen, method, status, received_at, slip_path, gateway_bill_id
payment_allocations	id, org_id, payment_id, invoice_id, amount_sen
gateway_bills	id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, status (pending, paid or failed)
audit_log	id, org_id, actor_id, action, entity_id, details, created_at
9. UI
Use shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS throughout, with toasts for every action (success and error), loading states instead of blank screens, and helpful messages for empty and invalid input. TypeScript in strict mode, without any.

Staff and managers:

A dashboard with the number of overdue invoices and the collections report for the last 6 months.
A list of leases, and a lease page with its invoices (period, due date, amount, paid, status) and payments (with a link to the slip for bank transfers).
Recording a payment: the amount typed in ringgit and parsed with parseRinggitToSen, the date and time received in Malaysia time, and a slip upload for bank transfers.
Managers approve or reject pending payments, and void approved ones (with a confirmation step and a reason).
Tenants:

Their lease, invoices with statuses, payments, and the amount due now.
Pay now, which shows the new gateway bill, and the /payments/return page.
Editing their phone number.
Every date and time is shown in Malaysia time, whatever the viewer's timezone (we check with a different browser timezone), without hydration warnings.

Part B - Code Review (REVIEW.md)
A teammate opened the pull request below. Review it in REVIEW.md. For each problem, give the line number(s), what goes wrong (a concrete scenario), how severe it is, and the fix, ordered from most to least severe. Report only real problems: every false positive costs points. If something looks suspicious but is correct, you may say so and explain why.

The rules of this brief apply. prisma connects to Postgres as the database owner. createClient() returns a Supabase server client for the current request. Assume allocate(tx, paymentId) is correct.

// app/api/leases/[leaseId]/late-fees/route.ts
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'
import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
 
const GRACE_DAYS = 7
const DAY_MS = 86_400_000
 
// Managers only. Adds a 2% late fee for each rent invoice still unpaid more than 7 days after its due date.
export async function POST(_req: Request, { params }: { params: Promise<{ leaseId: string }> }) {
  const supabase = await createClient()
  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
  if (user?.user_metadata.role !== 'manager') {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Forbidden' }, { status: 403 })
  }
 
  const { leaseId } = await params
  const lease = await prisma.lease.findUnique({
    where: { id: leaseId },
    include: { invoices: { include: { allocations: true } } },
  })
  if (!lease) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Not found' }, { status: 404 })
 
  const todayMyt = new Date(Date.now() + 8 * 3600 * 1000).toISOString().slice(0, 10)
  const cutoff = new Date(Date.parse(todayMyt) - GRACE_DAYS * DAY_MS)
 
  const fees = []
  for (const invoice of lease.invoices) {
    if (invoice.kind !== 'rent' || invoice.dueDate >= cutoff) continue
    const paid = invoice.allocations.reduce((sum, a) => sum + a.amountSen, 0n)
    if (Number(paid) / Number(invoice.amountSen) >= 0.995) continue
    const fee = Math.round((Number(invoice.amountSen - paid) * 2) / 100)
    fees.push(
      prisma.invoice.create({
        data: {
          orgId: lease.orgId,
          leaseId,
          kind: 'late_fee',
          dueDate: new Date(todayMyt),
          amountSen: BigInt(fee),
          reference: await nextReference(lease.orgId),
        },
      }),
    )
  }
  await Promise.all(fees)
  return NextResponse.json({ created: fees.length })
}
 
async function nextReference(orgId: string) {
  const last = await prisma.invoice.findFirst({ where: { orgId }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' } })
  return `INV-${(last ? parseInt(last.reference.slice(4), 10) : 0) + 1}`
}
 
// app/api/webhooks/gateway/route.ts
import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'
import { allocate } from '@/lib/allocation'
 
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const fields = Object.fromEntries(await req.formData()) as Record<string, string>
  const source = Object.keys(fields)
    .filter(k => k !== 'x_signature')
    .sort()
    .map(k => `${k}${fields[k]}`)
    .join('|')
  const expected = createHmac('sha256', process.env.GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY!).update(source).digest('hex')
  if (expected !== fields.x_signature) {
    console.error('Invalid signature', { fields, expected })
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid signature' }, { status: 401 })
  }
  if (fields.paid !== 'true') return NextResponse.json({ ok: true })
 
  const bill = await prisma.gatewayBill.findUnique({ where: { id: fields.id } })
  if (!bill) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unknown bill' }, { status: 404 })
  if (bill.status === 'paid') return NextResponse.json({ ok: true })
 
  await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.gatewayBill.update({ where: { id: bill.id }, data: { status: 'paid' } })
    const payment = await tx.payment.create({
      data: {
        orgId: bill.orgId,
        leaseId: bill.leaseId,
        method: 'online',
        status: 'approved',
        amountSen: BigInt(fields.paid_amount),
        receivedAt: new Date(),
        gatewayBillId: bill.id,
      },
    })
    await allocate(tx, payment.id)
  })
  return NextResponse.json({ ok: true })
}
 
// app/(staff)/dashboard/actions.ts
'use server'
import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'
 
// from and to are the first days of months, e.g. '2026-01-01'
export async function getCollections(orgId: string, from: string, to: string) {
  const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw<{ month: string; total: bigint }[]>`
    SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', received_at), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, SUM(amount_sen) AS total
    FROM payments
    WHERE org_id = ${orgId}::uuid AND status = 'approved'
      AND received_at >= ${from}::date AND received_at < ${to}::date + interval '1 month'
    GROUP BY 1
    ORDER BY 1`
  return rows.map(r => ({ month: r.month, collectedSen: Number(r.total) }))
}
Part C - Decisions (DECISIONS.md)
Answer each question in at most 150 words, pointing to files and line numbers in your repo:

Bonus (optional, only if done well)

Realtime updates on the tenant portal when a payment is settled.
Unit tests for lib/billing.ts and for allocation.
Server-side search and pagination for the leases list, synced with the URL.
Submission
GitHub URL: a public repo with your source, supabase/config.toml, supabase/migrations/, prisma/schema.prisma, the seed script, .env.example, REVIEW.md, DECISIONS.md, ai-logs/, and a README.md (how to run it, known issues, what you would do next). Do not commit real .env files.

Test account: manager@northwind.test, and the password all seeded accounts share.

How We Assess

Names are a contract. Table names, column names, endpoint paths, file paths and response shapes in this brief are what our tests use. You may add more of your own.
1. The Business
You are building part of the rent collection module of a property management platform used by Malaysian property management companies.

Each organization (a property management company) rents units to tenants under leases.
A lease produces invoices: an optional deposit, plus one rent invoice per monthly period.
Tenants pay by cash, by bank transfer (with an uploaded slip), or online through a payment gateway. Payments are allocated to invoices.
Business timezone: Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (UTC+8, no daylight saving). Currency: MYR (RM). 1 ringgit = 100 sen.
Your server runs in UTC and our assessors work from several timezones. Every date and time the app shows or accepts is Malaysia time, whatever the timezone of the server or of the viewer's device.
Roles
Role	Who	Can
manager	Organization admin	Everything in their organization: create leases, record payments (approved immediately), approve, reject and void payments, read the audit log
staff	Front desk	Read their organization's leases, invoices and payments; record payments (these wait for a manager's approval)
tenant	Renter	Read their own profile, leases, invoices and payments; update their own phone number; pay online
A staff member or manager belongs to exactly one organization. Nobody ever sees another organization's data.

2. Local Setup and Seed Data
Develop against a local Supabase stack (Docker and the Supabase CLI), not a cloud project. See Supabase local development. We grade by running your project on our machine from a fresh clone, with exactly these commands:

npx supabase start            # starts the stack from your supabase/config.toml
npx supabase db reset         # rebuilds the database from supabase/migrations/
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local    # we replace keys with the values from `npx supabase status` if they differ

npm run build && npm start
Commit supabase/config.toml, supabase/migrations/, and an .env.example that lists every variable your app needs, with local values and a comment saying where each one comes from.
npm run seed creates exactly the data below on a freshly reset database, through your normal code paths (your lease creation and payment logic), so the invoices and allocations it produces are the ones your app would produce.
All seeded accounts share one password of your choice, which you submit with your work.

Units and leases

Payments on Aisyah's lease

3. Billing Rules - lib/billing.ts
Create lib/billing.ts (or src/lib/billing.ts). It must be pure: no I/O, no imports from Next.js, React, Supabase or Prisma, and no dependence on the timezone of the machine it runs on. Your app must use it, and we test it directly.

export type InvoiceKind = 'deposit' | 'rent'
 
export interface ScheduledInvoice {
  kind: InvoiceKind
  periodIndex: number | null  // 0, 1, 2... for rent; null for the deposit
  periodStart: string | null  // 'YYYY-MM-DD'; null for the deposit
  periodEnd: string | null    // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive; null for the deposit
  dueDate: string             // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
  amountSen: number           // integer
}
 
export function generateSchedule(lease: {
  startDate: string           // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
  endDate: string             // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive (the tenant's last day)
  monthlyRentSen: number
  depositSen: number
}): ScheduledInvoice[]
 
export type InvoiceStatus = 'paid' | 'partially_paid' | 'unpaid' | 'overdue'
 
export function invoiceStatus(
  invoice: { dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number },
  now: Date,
): InvoiceStatus
 
export function parseRinggitToSen(input: string): number
generateSchedule
Validation. Throw an Error if a date is not a real calendar date written as YYYY-MM-DD, if endDate is before startDate, if monthlyRentSen is not a positive integer, or if depositSen is not a non-negative integer.
Deposit. If depositSen > 0, the first invoice is the deposit: kind: 'deposit', due on startDate, period fields null.
Anchors. Rent periods are anchored on the start date. The anchor of period k is the start date plus k calendar months, always counted from the start date (never from the previous anchor). If that month has fewer days than the start day, use the month's last day. A lease starting on Jan 31 has anchors Jan 31, Feb 28 (Feb 29 in leap years), Mar 31, Apr 30, and so on.
Periods. Period k runs from anchor k to the day before anchor k+1, and is due on anchor k. There is a period for every anchor on or before endDate.
Last period. It is cut at endDate. If it is shorter than its full length, it costs monthlyRentSen x days used / days in the full period, rounded half up to the nearest sen. Every other period costs monthlyRentSen.
Order. The deposit first, then rent by period index.
Worked example (Aisyah's lease):

Period	Kind	Dates	Due	Amount
deposit		2026-01-31	RM 3,000.00
0	rent	2026-01-31 to 2026-02-27	2026-01-31	RM 1,500.00
1	rent	2026-02-28 to 2026-03-30	2026-02-28	RM 1,500.00
2	rent	2026-03-31 to 2026-04-29	2026-03-31	RM 1,500.00
3	rent	2026-04-30 to 2026-05-30	2026-04-30	RM 1,500.00
4	rent	2026-05-31 to 2026-06-29	2026-05-31	RM 1,500.00
5	rent	2026-06-30 to 2026-07-15	2026-06-30	RM 774.19
Period 5 uses 16 of the 31 days from 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-30: 150000 x 16 / 31 = 77419.35, so 77419 sen.

invoiceStatus
Apply these rules in order:

paid if paidSen >= amountSen.
overdue if today's Malaysia date is after dueDate. An invoice due 2026-03-01 becomes overdue at 2026-03-02 00:00 Malaysia time (2026-03-01T16:00:00Z), not a moment earlier.
partially_paid if paidSen > 0.
Otherwise unpaid.
parseRinggitToSen
Turns what a user types into sen. It accepts digits with optional comma thousands separators (groups of exactly three digits) and an optional decimal part of one or two digits, ignoring whitespace around the value: "1,500.50" gives 150050, "1.15" gives 115, "7" gives 700. Anything else throws an Error, for example "", "-5", "1.234", "1e3", "RM 10", "1,23".

4. Payments
Recording a payment
Staff and managers record cash or bank transfer payments on a lease: the amount, the method, and the date and time the money was received (entered and shown in Malaysia time).
A bank transfer needs a slip: a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 5 MB, stored in Supabase Storage (section 6). If recording fails after the upload, the file must not be left behind.
A payment recorded by a manager is approved immediately. A payment recorded by staff is pending_verification until a manager approves or rejects it.
Cap. A new payment may not be more than the lease's remaining balance (the total of all its invoices minus everything allocated to them) minus the total of the lease's payments still pending_verification. Paying future periods in advance is allowed within the cap.
Approving, rejecting and voiding (managers only)
Approve a pending_verification payment. At that moment, check again that it is not more than the lease's remaining balance. If it is, refuse and leave it pending.
Reject a pending_verification payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters.
Void an approved payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters. Voiding removes that payment's allocations. Other payments' allocations do not change.
Payments are never deleted. Every approval, rejection, void and lease creation writes a row to audit_log (who, what, when, details).
Allocation
When a payment becomes approved, its amount is allocated to the lease's invoices that still have something unpaid, in this order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index. Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one, including invoices that are not due yet. Whatever is left once every invoice is fully paid is stored on the payment as unapplied_sen. Only online payments can end up with an unapplied amount, because manual payments are capped.

The paid amount of an invoice is the sum of its allocations. Statuses are computed with invoiceStatus, never stored.

All of this must stay correct when requests arrive at the same time. For example, two staff members recording payments on the same lease at once must not exceed the cap together, and a payment approved twice at once is allocated once.

Collections report
The total of approved payments for each calendar month of received_at in Malaysia time, over a range of months, including months with nothing collected. With the seed data, Northwind's report for 2026-01 to 2026-03 is [{ month: '2026-01', collectedSen: 300000 }, { month: '2026-02', collectedSen: 0 }, { month: '2026-03', collectedSen: 200000 }].

5. Online Payments
A tenant pays online like this:

The tenant clicks Pay now on their lease. Your API creates a gateway bill for the amount due now: the unpaid amounts of the lease's invoices due on or before today's Malaysia date. If nothing is due, refuse. Bill ids must be impossible to guess.
In production the tenant would now be redirected to the gateway. In this test, show the bill id and amount: we play the gateway using the simulator below.
The gateway calls your webhook, POST /api/webhooks/gateway. Only the webhook can settle a bill. The gateway also sends the tenant back to /payments/return?bill_id=...&paid=true. That page only shows the bill's real status from your database and changes nothing.
Webhook
The request body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with these fields. The gateway may add more fields in future.

Field	Example	Notes
id	bill_8f3a2c	Your bill id (this short example is guessable; yours must not be)
paid	true	true or false
paid_amount	210050	Amount in sen; 0 when not paid
paid_at	2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800	When it was paid
transaction_id	TX-000123	Gateway transaction id
transaction_status	completed	completed, failed or pending
x_signature	06994f...	See below
Signature. Take every field in the request except x_signature, sort them by key (ascending by character code), write each one as the key immediately followed by the value, join them with |, and compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the resulting string with your secret key GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY, as lowercase hex. Test vector, with the key test_x_signature_key and the six example values above:

source:    idbill_8f3a2c|paidtrue|paid_amount210050|paid_at2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800|transaction_idTX-000123|transaction_statuscompleted
signature: 06994fab2d674e7829144eaa2204631716d3c099b503d38945e92b6296531641
Required behavior:

Situation	Response	Effect
Signature missing or wrong	401	None
Unknown bill id	404	None
paid=true and paid_amount is not the bill's amount	422	None
paid=true, bill pending or failed	200	Bill becomes paid, and one approved online payment is created with received_at = paid_at, then allocated
paid=true, bill already paid (a repeat delivery)	200	None
paid=false, bill pending	200	Bill becomes failed
paid=false, bill already failed (a repeat delivery)	200	None
paid=false, bill already paid (late or out of order)	200	None: a paid bill never goes back
The gateway retries, so it may deliver the same callback several times, including at the same moment. A bill creates at most one payment, ever. Never log the secret key or whole callback payloads.

Simulator
Save this as gateway-sim.mjs and run node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false] with GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY set.

import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'
 
const [billId, amountSen, paid = 'true'] = process.argv.slice(2)
const url = process.env.WEBHOOK_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway'
const key = process.env.GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY
 
const myt = new Date(Date.now() + 8 * 3600 * 1000).toISOString()
const fields = {
  id: billId,
  paid,
  paid_amount: paid === 'true' ? amountSen : '0',
  paid_at: `${myt.slice(0, 10)} ${myt.slice(11, 19)} +0800`,
  transaction_id: `TX-${Date.now()}`,
  transaction_status: paid === 'true' ? 'completed' : 'failed',
}
const source = Object.keys(fields).sort().map(k => `${k}${fields[k]}`).join('|')
fields.x_signature = createHmac('sha256', key).update(source).digest('hex')
 
const res = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
  body: new URLSearchParams(fields),
})
console.log(res.status, await res.text())
6. Access Control
Access is enforced in two places, and we test both:

Your server code: route handlers, Server Actions and server components. Every endpoint must authenticate the caller and check their organization and role itself. A protected page or a hidden button is not a check.
The Supabase Data API and Storage, which anyone holding your publishable key can call directly with their own access token.
Server code
Roles come from your memberships table, and from tenants.user_id for tenants. Never take a role or an organization from anything the user can edit, such as user_metadata.
On the server, authenticate with supabase.auth.getUser() or getClaims(), not getSession().
A request about a record in another organization, or another tenant's record, gets 404: do not reveal that it exists. A request about a record the caller can see, for an action their role does not allow, gets 403. A request without a valid login gets 401.
IDs in request bodies are untrusted too. For example, a manager must not be able to create a lease on another organization's unit or tenant.
Our tests call your API with Authorization: Bearer <access token>, where the token is a Supabase access token for one of the seeded users. Accept that header as well as the normal session cookie.
The service role (secret) key must never reach the browser.
Data API
This table is the most access allowed through the Supabase Data API, which is PostgREST called with a user's token. Granting less is fine where your app does not need it, with one exception: the tenant portal reads the tenant's own data, and updates their phone number, directly from the browser with supabase-js.

Table	anon	tenant	staff	manager
organizations	none	read own organization	read own organization	read own organization
memberships	none	none	read own organization	read own organization
units	none	read the units of own leases	read own organization	read own organization
tenants	none	read own row, update only phone	read own organization	read own organization
leases, invoices, payments, payment_allocations, gateway_bills	none	read the rows of own leases	read own organization	read own organization
audit_log	none	none	none	read own organization
Every other insert, update or delete through the Data API must fail for everyone. This covers every table, view and function (/rest/v1/rpc/...) you create, not just the ones above. audit_log is append-only for every role, including the service role and the database owner.

Storage
Bank transfer slips go in a private bucket named payment-slips, under <org_id>/.... Only staff and managers of that organization can upload there, and they read slips through short-lived signed URLs. Tenants, other organizations and anonymous users cannot read, list or upload slips. A payment's slip_path must point to an existing file in its own organization's folder.

7. HTTP API
Request and response bodies are JSON, except for the webhook. Amounts are integers in sen. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and instants are ISO 8601 with an offset. Errors return { "error": "message" }.

Method and path	Who	Success	Other responses
POST /api/leases	manager	201 { id }	400 invalid input, 409 overlaps another lease on the unit
GET /api/leases/:leaseId	staff, manager, the lease's tenant	200, shape below	
POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments	staff, manager	201 { id, status }	400 invalid input, 422 over the cap
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/approve	manager	200 { status }	409 not pending, 422 over the remaining balance
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject	manager	200 { status }	400 missing reason, 409 not pending
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void	manager	200 { status }	400 missing reason, 409 not approved
POST /api/leases/:leaseId/gateway-bills	the lease's tenant	201 { billId, amountSen }	422 nothing due
GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM	staff, manager	200 [{ month: 'YYYY-MM', collectedSen }], one entry per month in order	400 invalid range
POST /api/webhooks/gateway	the gateway	see section 5	
Every endpoint also returns 401, 403 and 404 as described in section 6. Request bodies:

// POST /api/leases
{ unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
 
// POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments
{ amountSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer'; receivedAt: string; slipPath?: string }
 
// POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject and POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void
{ reason: string }
GET /api/leases/:leaseId returns the invoices in allocation order:

{
  lease: { id: string; unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
  invoices: {
    id: string; kind: 'deposit' | 'rent'; periodIndex: number | null; periodStart: string | null; periodEnd: string | null
    dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number; status: InvoiceStatus
  }[]
  payments: {
    id: string; amountSen: number; unappliedSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer' | 'online'
    status: 'pending_verification' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'voided'; receivedAt: string
  }[]
}
Creating a lease stores the lease and exactly the invoices generateSchedule returns, all or nothing. Leases on the same unit never overlap (both dates are inclusive), even when two requests arrive at the same moment.

8. Database
Keep every database object in SQL migrations under supabase/migrations/: tables, constraints, RLS policies, grants, functions, triggers, and the storage bucket and its policies. npx supabase db reset must rebuild all of it; nothing may depend on changes made by hand in Supabase Studio. Use Prisma for server-side data access, with prisma/schema.prisma matching the database.
Store money as integer sen (bigint), never as a floating-point type. Calendar dates are date, and instants are timestamptz.
Required tables and columns (add whatever else you need):
Table	Required columns
organizations	id, name
memberships	user_id, org_id, role (manager or staff)
